b is an element of the universal set
a is less than or equal to b
conclusions: a is an element of the universal set
function_body: theorem isLowerSet_univ : IsLowerSet (univ : Set α) := fun _ _ _ => id

name: IsUpperSet.compl
description: Given an upper set s, this tool proves that its complement is a lower set.
conclusions: sᶜ (the complement of s) is a lower set
function_body: theorem IsUpperSet.compl (hs : IsUpperSet s) : IsLowerSet sᶜ := fun _a _b h hb ha => hb <| hs h ha

name: IsLowerSet.compl
description: A tool to prove that the complement of a lower set is an upper set.
function_body: theorem IsLowerSet.compl (hs : IsLowerSet s) : IsUpperSet sᶜ := fun _a _b h hb ha => hb <| hs h ha

name: nonempty_invertible_iff_isUnit
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between invertibility and being a unit in the context of monoids.
conditions: a is an element of α
conclusions: a is invertible if and only if a is a unit
function_body:
theorem nonempty_invertible_iff_isUnit [Monoid α] (a : α) : Nonempty (Invertible a) ↔ IsUnit a :=
  ⟨Nonempty.rec <| @isUnit_of_invertible _ _ _, IsUnit.nonempty_invertible⟩

name: invOf_neg
description: This tool verifies that in a monoid with negative inverses, the inverse of a negated invertible element is the negation of the inverse of the element.
conditions: a is invertible in a monoid
conclusions: The inverse of -a is equal to the negation of the inverse of a
function_body: theorem invOf_neg [Monoid α] [HasDistribNeg α] (a : α) [Invertible a] [Invertible (-a)] : ⅟ (-a) = -⅟ a := invOf_eq_right_inv (by simp)

name: one_sub_invOf_two
description: A tool that proves the equality 1 - 1/2 = 1/2 in a ring where 2 is invertible.
function_body:
theorem one_sub_invOf_two [Ring α] [Invertible (2 : α)] : 1 - (⅟ 2 : α) = ⅟ 2 :=
  (isUnit_of_invertible (2 : α)).mul_right_inj.1 <| by
    rw [mul_sub, mul_invOf_self, mul_one, ← one_add_one_eq_two, add_sub_cancel]

name: invOf_two_add_invOf_two
description: This tool proves that in any non-associative semiring where 2 is invertible, the inverse of 2 added to itself is equal to 1.
conclusions: The inverse of 2 added to itself is equal to 1
function_body:
theorem invOf_two_add_invOf_two [NonAssocSemiring α] [Invertible (2 : α)] :
    (⅟ 2 : α) + (⅟ 2 : α) = 1 := by rw [← two_mul, mul_invOf_self]

name: Commute.invOf_right
description: This tool proves that if two elements a and b commute, then a and the inverse of b also commute in a monoid with an invertible element b.
conditions: b is invertible in the monoid
function_body:
theorem Commute.invOf_right [Monoid α] {a b : α} [Invertible b] (h : Commute a b) :
  Commute a (⅟ b) :=
calc
  a * ⅟ b = ⅟ b * (b * a * ⅟ b) := by simp [mul_assoc]
  _ = ⅟ b * (a * b * ⅟ b) := by rw [h.eq]
  _ = ⅟ b * a := by simp [mul_assoc]

name: Commute.invOf_left
description: A theorem that proves if a monoid element a commutes with an invertible element b, then a also commutes with the inverse of b.
conditions: a and b are elements of α
conclusions: a commutes with the inverse of b (a commutes with b^(-1))
function_body:
theorem Commute.invOf_left [Monoid α] {a b : α} [Invertible b] (h : Commute b a) : Commute (⅟ b) a :=
  calc
    ⅟ b * a = ⅟ b * (a * b * ⅟ b) := by simp [mul_assoc]
    _ = ⅟ b * (b * a * ⅟ b) := by rw [h.eq]
    _ = a * ⅟ b := by simp [mul_assoc]

name: commute_invOf
description: A tool to prove that for any element m of a monoid with identity, the inverse of m commutes with m.
conditions: M is a type with an identity element 1
m is an element of M
function_body:
theorem commute_invOf {M : Type*} [One M] [Mul M] (m : M) [Invertible m] : Commute m (⅟ m) :=
  calc
    m * ⅟ m = 1 := mul_invOf_self m
    _ = ⅟ m * m := (invOf_mul_self m).symm

name: pos_of_invertible_cast
description: This tool determines that a natural number n, which is invertible in a nontrivial semiring, must be positive.
conditions: n is invertible in a nontrivial semiring
function_body:
theorem pos_of_invertible_cast [Semiring α] [Nontrivial α] (n : ℕ) [Invertible (n : α)] : 0 < n :=
  Nat.zero_lt_of_ne_zero fun h => nonzero_of_invertible (n : α) (h ▸ Nat.cast_zero)

name: Ring.inverse_invertible
description: This tool proves that the inverse of an invertible element is equal to the reciprocal of that element in a ring.
conclusions: The inverse of x is equal to 1/x
function_body:
theorem Ring.inverse_invertible (x : α) [Invertible x] : Ring.inverse x = ⅟ x :=
  Ring.inverse_unit (unitOfInvertible _)

name: div_mul_cancel_of_invertible
description: This theorem states that if b is invertible, then dividing a by b and multiplying the result by b yields the original number a.
function_body: theorem div_mul_cancel_of_invertible (a b : α) [Invertible b] : a / b * b = a := div_mul_cancel a (nonzero_of_invertible b)

name: mul_div_cancel_of_invertible
description: This tool states that for any elements a and b from a group, if b is invertible, then the product of a and b divided by b equals a.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group
function_body:
theorem mul_div_cancel_of_invertible (a b : α) [Invertible b] : a * b / b = a :=
  mul_div_cancel a (nonzero_of_invertible b)

name: div_self_of_invertible
description: A tool to prove that an invertible element in a group divides itself if and only if it equals the identity element.
conditions: a is an invertible element in a group
conclusions: a divides itself if and only if a = 1
function_body:
theorem div_self_of_invertible (a : α) [Invertible a] : a / a = 1 :=
  div_self (nonzero_of_invertible a)

name: invOf_div
description: Given that both 'a' and 'b' are invertible elements, this tool proves that the inverse of 'a' divided by 'b' is 'b' divided by 'a'.
conclusions: The inverse of 'a / b' is 'b / a'
function_body: theorem invOf_div (a b : α) [Invertible a] [Invertible b] [Invertible (a / b)] : ⅟ (a / b) = b / a := invOf_eq_right_inv (by simp [← mul_div_assoc])

name: map_invOf
description: This tool proves that the image of an invertible element under a monoid homomorphism is the inverse of the image of the element.
conditions: F is a monoid homomorphism from R to S
r is an invertible element in R
function_body: theorem map_invOf {R : Type*} {S : Type*} {F : Type*} [MulOneClass R] [Monoid S] [MonoidHomClass F R S] (f : F) (r : R) [Invertible r] [ifr : Invertible (f r)] : f (⅟ r) = ⅟ (f r) := have h : ifr = Invertible.map f r := Subsingleton.elim _ _ by subst h; rfl

name: AddCommGroupCat.image.fac
description: This tool ensures the factorization of a morphism through its image in the context of additive commutative groups.
conditions: There is a morphism f: A → B
There exist definitions of factorThruImage and image.ι for the morphism f
The morphism f can be factorized as an epimorphism (epi) followed by a monomorphism (mono)
conclusions: The equation factorThruImage(f) ≫ image.ι(f) = f holds
function_body:
theorem image.fac : factorThruImage f ≫ image.ι f = f := by
  ext
  rfl

name: AddCommGroupCat.image.lift_fac
description: This theorem shows that for any monofactorisation F' of a morphism f, the composition of image.lift F' and F'.m equals the image inclusion of f.
conditions: F' is a MonoFactorisation of f
function_body:
theorem image.lift_fac (F' : MonoFactorisation f) : image.lift F' ≫ F'.m = image.ι f := by
  ext x
  change (F'.e ≫ F'.m) _ = _
  rw [F'.fac, (Classical.indefiniteDescription _ x.2).2]
  rfl

name: commutatorElement_def
description: A tool that defines the commutator of two elements in a group.
conditions: g₁ and g₂ are elements of a group G
conclusions: The commutator of g₁ and g₂ is g₁ * g₂ * g₁⁻¹ * g₂⁻¹
function_body:
theorem commutatorElement_def {G : Type*} [Group G] (g₁ g₂ : G) :
    ⁅g₁, g₂⁆ = g₁ * g₂ * g₁⁻¹ * g₂⁻¹ :=
  rfl

name: zero_pow
description: This tool proves that for any natural number n > 0, 0 raised to the power n equals 0.
function_body:
theorem zero_pow : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → (0 : M) ^ n = 0
  | n + 1, _ => by rw [pow_succ, zero_mul]

name: zero_pow'
description: This tool proves that for any nonzero natural number n, raising 0 to the power of n results in 0.
conditions: n is a nonzero natural number
function_body:
theorem zero_pow' : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → (0 : ℕ) ^ n = 0
  | 0, h => absurd rfl h
  | k + 1, _ => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact zero_mul _

name: zero_pow_eq
description: This tool determines the value of 0 raised to the power of n, given different conditions for n being zero, positive, or negative.
conclusions: If n is negative, then 0^n is undefined
function_body:
theorem zero_pow_eq (n : ℕ) : (0 : M) ^ n = if n = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
  split_ifs with h
  · rw [h, pow_zero]
  · rw [zero_pow (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h)]

name: pow_eq_zero_of_le
description: This tool verifies that if a power of an element is zero and the exponent is less than or equal to another exponent, then the power of the element with the larger exponent is also zero.
function_body:
theorem pow_eq_zero_of_le {x : M} {n m : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ m) (hx : x ^ n = 0) : x ^ m = 0 := by
  rw [← tsub_add_cancel_of_le hn, pow_add, hx, mul_zero]

name: pow_eq_zero
description: This tool proves that if the n-th power of an element x equals zero in a ring with no zero divisors, then x must be zero.
conditions: Ring R has no zero divisors
function_body:
theorem pow_eq_zero [NoZeroDivisors M] {x : M} {n : ℕ} (H : x ^ n = 0) : x = 0 := by
  induction' n with n ih
  · rw [pow_zero] at H
    rw [← mul_one x, H, mul_zero]
  · rw [pow_succ] at H
    exact Or.casesOn (mul_eq_zero.1 H) id ih

name: pow_eq_zero_iff
description: This tool proves that for an element 'a' in a domain 'M' and a positive integer 'n', the equality 'a^n = 0' holds if and only if 'a = 0'.
conditions: a is an element of a domain M
conclusions: a^n = 0 if and only if a = 0
function_body:
theorem pow_eq_zero_iff [NoZeroDivisors M] {a : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : a ^ n = 0 ↔ a = 0 := by
  refine' ⟨pow_eq_zero, _⟩
  rintro rfl
  exact zero_pow hn

name: pow_eq_zero_iff'
description:
A tool to determine whether \(a^n = 0\) if and only if \(a = 0\) and \(n 
e 0\) in a ring without zero divisors.
conditions: M is a ring without zero divisors
a is an element of M
function_body: theorem pow_eq_zero_iff' [NoZeroDivisors M] [Nontrivial M] {a : M} {n : ℕ} : a ^ n = 0 ↔ a = 0 ∧ n ≠ 0 := by cases (zero_le n).eq_or_gt <;> simp [*, ne_of_gt]

name: pow_ne_zero_iff
description: This tool verifies that for any element in a ring with no zero divisors, raising the element to a positive power results in a non-zero value if and only if the element itself is non-zero.
conditions: M is a ring with no zero divisors
a is an element in M
n is a positive natural number
function_body:
theorem pow_ne_zero_iff [NoZeroDivisors M] {a : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : a ^ n ≠ 0 ↔ a ≠ 0 :=
  (pow_eq_zero_iff hn).not

name: ne_zero_pow
description: This tool uses the given theorem to deduce that if a mathematical object raised to a non-zero natural number power is not zero, then the object itself must also be non-zero.
conditions: n is a non-zero natural number
function_body:
theorem ne_zero_pow {a : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ^ n ≠ 0 → a ≠ 0 := by
  contrapose!
  rintro rfl
  exact zero_pow' n hn

name: pow_ne_zero
description: A tool that proves if a structure has no zero divisors, then raising any nonzero element to any natural number power will not result in zero.
conditions: M is a structure with no zero divisors.
a is an element of M.
function_body:
theorem pow_ne_zero [NoZeroDivisors M] {a : M} (n : ℕ) (h : a ≠ 0) : a ^ n ≠ 0 :=
  mt pow_eq_zero h

name: sq_eq_zero_iff
description: A theorem that asserts, in a ring with no zero divisors, an element squared equals zero if and only if the element itself is zero.
conditions: The ring R has no zero divisors.
conclusions: x^2 = 0 if and only if x = 0.
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_zero_iff [NoZeroDivisors M] {a : M} : a ^ 2 = 0 ↔ a = 0 :=
  pow_eq_zero_iff two_pos

name: zero_pow_eq_zero
description: This tool establishes that for any number n in a non-trivial monoid, 0^n = 0 if and only if n > 0.
function_body:
theorem zero_pow_eq_zero [Nontrivial M] {n : ℕ} : (0 : M) ^ n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by
  constructor <;> intro h
  · rw [pos_iff_ne_zero]
    rintro rfl
    simp at h
  · exact zero_pow' n h.ne.symm

name: Ring.inverse_pow
description: This tool provides a theorem stating that in a ring, for all positive integers n, the nth power of the inverse of an element is equal to the inverse of the nth power of the element.
conditions: r is an element of a ring
conclusions: r^(-n) = (r^(-1))^n for all positive integers n
function_body:
theorem Ring.inverse_pow (r : M) : ∀ n : ℕ, Ring.inverse r ^ n = Ring.inverse (r ^ n)
  | 0 => by rw [pow_zero, pow_zero, Ring.inverse_one]
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ, pow_succ', Ring.mul_inverse_rev' ((Commute.refl r).pow_left n),
      Ring.inverse_pow r n]

name: coe_powMonoidWithZeroHom
description: A theorem that defines the homomorphism which maps each element of a monoid to its n-th power.
conditions: The structure must be a monoid.
conclusions: powMonoidWithZeroHom maps each element of the monoid to its n-th power.
function_body: theorem coe_powMonoidWithZeroHom : (powMonoidWithZeroHom hn : M → M) = fun x ↦ (x^n : M) := rfl

name: powMonoidWithZeroHom_apply
description: This theorem states that in a monoid with zero, raising an element to the power of n (using monoid's power notation) is equivalent to repeatedly applying the element n times.
conditions: M is a monoid with zero
a is an element in the monoid M
function_body:
theorem powMonoidWithZeroHom_apply (a : M) : powMonoidWithZeroHom hn a = a ^ n :=
  rfl

name: pow_dvd_pow_iff
description: Determines the conditions under which a power of an element in a cancel-commutative monoid with zero divides another power of the same element.
conditions: R is a cancel-commutative monoid with zero
x is a nonzero element in R
x is not a unit in R
conclusions: x^n divides x^m if and only if n ≤ m
function_body:
theorem pow_dvd_pow_iff [CancelCommMonoidWithZero R] {x : R} {n m : ℕ} (h0 : x ≠ 0)
    (h1 : ¬IsUnit x) : x ^ n ∣ x ^ m ↔ n ≤ m := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [← not_lt]
    intro hmn
    apply h1
    have : x ^ m * x ∣ x ^ m * 1 := by
      rw [← pow_succ', mul_one]
      exact (pow_dvd_pow _ (Nat.succ_le_of_lt hmn)).trans h
    rwa [mul_dvd_mul_iff_left, ← isUnit_iff_dvd_one] at this
    apply pow_ne_zero m h0
  · apply pow_dvd_pow

name: RingHom.map_pow
description: This theorem states that if f is a ring homomorphism and a is an element in the ring R, then for any natural number n, the image of a^n under f is equal to the image of a under f raised to the power n.
conditions: a is an element in the ring R
conclusions: f(a^n) = f(a)^n for any natural number n
function_body:
theorem RingHom.map_pow (f : R →+* S) (a) : ∀ n : ℕ, f (a ^ n) = f a ^ n :=
  map_pow f a

name: min_pow_dvd_add
description: A tool that states if c raised to n divides a and c raised to m divides b, then c raised to the minimum of n and m divides a + b.
function_body:
theorem min_pow_dvd_add {n m : ℕ} {a b c : R} (ha : c ^ n ∣ a) (hb : c ^ m ∣ b) :
    c ^ min n m ∣ a + b := by
  replace ha := (pow_dvd_pow c (min_le_left n m)).trans ha
  replace hb := (pow_dvd_pow c (min_le_right n m)).trans hb
  exact dvd_add ha hb

name: add_sq
description: This tool expands the square of a sum of two real numbers.
conditions: a and b are real numbers
function_body:
theorem add_sq (a b : R) : (a + b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + 2 * a * b + b ^ 2 := by
  simp only [sq, add_mul_self_eq]

name: add_sq'
description: This tool proves that the square of a sum of two terms is equal to the sum of the squares of the terms plus twice their product.
conditions: a and b are elements of a ring R
function_body:
theorem add_sq' (a b : R) : (a + b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 2 * a * b := by
  rw [add_sq, add_assoc, add_comm _ (b ^ 2), add_assoc]

name: neg_one_pow_eq_or
description: This tool confirms that for any natural number n, (-1)^n is either 1 or -1 using mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem neg_one_pow_eq_or : ∀ n : ℕ, (-1 : R) ^ n = 1 ∨ (-1 : R) ^ n = -1
  | 0 => Or.inl (pow_zero _)
  | n + 1 => (neg_one_pow_eq_or n).symm.imp
    (fun h ↦ by rw [pow_succ, h, neg_one_mul, neg_neg])
    (fun h ↦ by rw [pow_succ, h, mul_one])

name: neg_pow'
description: This tool proves the property of exponents that raising a negative number to a power is equivalent to the positive number raised to the same power times (-1) raised to that power.
function_body:
theorem neg_pow' (a : R) (n : ℕ) : (-a) ^ n = a ^ n * (-1) ^ n :=
  mul_neg_one a ▸ (Commute.neg_one_right a).mul_pow n

name: neg_pow_bit0
description: This tool verifies that raising the negation of a ring element to the power of a power of two is equivalent to raising the element itself to that power.
conditions: a is an element of a ring
function_body:
theorem neg_pow_bit0 (a : R) (n : ℕ) : (-a) ^ bit0 n = a ^ bit0 n := by
  rw [pow_bit0', neg_mul_neg, pow_bit0']

name: neg_pow_n
description: This theorem shows that raising the negation of a real number to a natural number exponent yields the negation of raising the number itself to the same exponent.
conditions: a is an arbitrary real number
function_body:
theorem neg_pow_n (a : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : (-a) ^ n = -a ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n' ih => simp [pow_succ, ih, neg_mul_eq_neg_mul]

name: neg_sq
description: This tool states that the square of the negation of any real number is equal to the square of that number.
function_body: theorem neg_sq (a : R) : (-a) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 := by simp [sq]

name: neg_one_sq
description: This tool proves that the square of negative one is equal to one.
function_body: theorem neg_one_sq : (-1 : R) ^ 2 = 1 := by simp [neg_sq, one_pow]

name: Commute.sq_sub_sq
description: This tool verifies that given two elements a and b that commute (i.e., ab = ba), the expression a^2 - b^2 equals (a + b)(a - b).
function_body:
theorem Commute.sq_sub_sq (h : Commute a b) : a ^ 2 - b ^ 2 = (a + b) * (a - b) := by
  rw [sq, sq, h.mul_self_sub_mul_self_eq]

name: neg_one_pow_mul_eq_zero_iff
description: This theorem states that the product of (-1) raised to any integer power and a real number r equals 0 if and only if r itself equals 0.
conditions: r is a real number (r ∈ ℝ)
conclusions: (-1)^n * r = 0 if and only if r = 0
function_body:
theorem neg_one_pow_mul_eq_zero_iff {n : ℕ} {r : R} : (-1) ^ n * r = 0 ↔ r = 0 := by
  rcases neg_one_pow_eq_or R n with h | h <;> simp [h]

name: mul_neg_one_pow_eq_zero_iff
description: This tool determines that for any real number r and natural number n, r multiplied by (-1) raised to the nth power equals zero if and only if r equals zero.
function_body:
theorem mul_neg_one_pow_eq_zero_iff {n : ℕ} {r : R} : r * (-1) ^ n = 0 ↔ r = 0 := by
  rcases neg_one_pow_eq_or R n with h | h <;> simp [h]

name: Commute.sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg
description: This tool determines whether two elements in a group are equal or negatives of each other, given that their squares are equal and they commute.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group
conclusions: a^2 = b^2 if and only if a = b or a = -b
function_body:
theorem Commute.sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg (h : Commute a b) :
    a ^ 2 = b ^ 2 ↔ a = b ∨ a = -b := by
  rw [← sub_eq_zero, h.sq_sub_sq, mul_eq_zero, add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg, sub_eq_zero, or_comm]

name: sq_eq_one_iff
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that states a number 'a' squared equals 1 if and only if 'a' is either 1 or -1.
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_one_iff : a ^ 2 = 1 ↔ a = 1 ∨ a = -1 := by
  rw [← (Commute.one_right a).sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg, one_pow]

name: sq_ne_one_iff
description: This theorem determines that a number's square is not equal to 1 if and only if the number itself is neither 1 nor -1.
function_body:
theorem sq_ne_one_iff : a ^ 2 ≠ 1 ↔ a ≠ 1 ∧ a ≠ -1 :=
  sq_eq_one_iff.not.trans not_or

name: sq_sub_sq
description: This tool proves that the difference of the squares of two real numbers is equal to the product of their sum and difference based on the given theorem.
conditions: a and b are real numbers
function_body:
theorem sq_sub_sq (a b : R) : a ^ 2 - b ^ 2 = (a + b) * (a - b) :=
  (Commute.all a b).sq_sub_sq

name: sub_sq
description: This tool proves that the square of the difference of two real numbers is equal to the square of the first number minus twice the product of the two numbers plus the square of the second number.
function_body:
theorem sub_sq (a b : R) : (a - b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 - 2 * a * b + b ^ 2 := by
  rw [sub_eq_add_neg, add_sq, neg_sq, mul_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg]

name: sub_sq'
description: This tool verifies the difference of squares formula, which states that the square of (a - b) equals a^2 + b^2 - 2ab.
conditions: a and b are real numbers
function_body:
theorem sub_sq' (a b : R) : (a - b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 - 2 * a * b := by
  rw [sub_eq_add_neg, add_sq', neg_sq, mul_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg]

name: sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg
description: A tool to verify or conclude that for real numbers a and b, a^2 = b^2 if and only if a = b or a = -b.
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg : a ^ 2 = b ^ 2 ↔ a = b ∨ a = -b :=
  (Commute.all a b).sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg

name: eq_or_eq_neg_of_sq_eq_sq
description: This tool determines that if the squares of two numbers are equal, then the numbers are either equal or opposites.
function_body:
theorem eq_or_eq_neg_of_sq_eq_sq (a b : R) : a ^ 2 = b ^ 2 → a = b ∨ a = -b :=
  sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg.1

name: Units.sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg
description: This tool verifies that for any two real numbers 'a' and 'b', if the squares of 'a' and 'b' are equal, then 'a' is either equal to 'b' or '-b'.
conditions: a and b are real numbers
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg {a b : Rˣ} : a ^ 2 = b ^ 2 ↔ a = b ∨ a = -b := by
  simp_rw [ext_iff, val_pow_eq_pow_val, sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg, Units.val_neg]

name: Units.eq_or_eq_neg_of_sq_eq_sq
description: This tool provides a proof that for nonzero real numbers a and b, if their squares are equal, then a is either equal to b or equal to the negative of b.
conditions: a and b are nonzero real numbers
function_body:
theorem eq_or_eq_neg_of_sq_eq_sq (a b : Rˣ) (h : a ^ 2 = b ^ 2) : a = b ∨ a = -b :=
  Units.sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg.1 h

name: IsConj.refl
description: A tool that proves any element in a group is conjugate to itself.
conditions: a is an element of a group
function_body:
theorem IsConj.refl (a : α) : IsConj a a :=
  ⟨1, SemiconjBy.one_left a⟩

name: IsConj.symm
description: This tool verifies that if one element is conjugate to another, then the second element is conjugate to the first, given the type has an involution.
conditions: a and b are elements of a type with an involution.
function_body:
theorem IsConj.symm {a b : α} : IsConj a b → IsConj b a
  | ⟨c, hc⟩ => ⟨c⁻¹, hc.units_inv_symm_left⟩

name: isConj_comm
description: This tool verifies the commutativity of the conjugation relation in a group, confirming that if one element is conjugate to another, the reverse is also true.
conditions: g and h are elements of a group
conclusions: g and h are conjugate if and only if h and g are conjugate
function_body: theorem isConj_comm {g h : α} : IsConj g h ↔ IsConj h g := ⟨IsConj.symm, IsConj.symm⟩

name: IsConj.trans
description: This tool provides a method to determine if two elements are conjugate based on their relationship with an intermediate element.
function_body:
theorem IsConj.trans {a b c : α} : IsConj a b → IsConj b c → IsConj a c
  | ⟨c₁, hc₁⟩, ⟨c₂, hc₂⟩ => ⟨c₂ * c₁, hc₂.mul_left hc₁⟩

name: isConj_iff_eq
description: A tool to determine that two elements in a commutative monoid are conjugates if and only if they are equal.
conditions: a and b are elements of a commutative monoid
there exists an element c such that a = c^{-1} b c, if they are conjugates
conclusions: a and b are equal if and only if they are conjugates
function_body:
theorem isConj_iff_eq {α : Type*} [CommMonoid α] {a b : α} : IsConj a b ↔ a = b :=
  ⟨fun ⟨c, hc⟩ => by
    rw [SemiconjBy, mul_comm, ← Units.mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul, mul_assoc, c.mul_inv, mul_one] at hc
    exact hc, fun h => by rw [h]⟩

name: MonoidHom.map_isConj
description: This tool demonstrates that if two elements are conjugate in the domain of a monoid homomorphism, their images under the homomorphism are conjugate in the codomain.
conditions: c, a, b are elements in α
function_body:
theorem MonoidHom.map_isConj (f : α →* β) {a b : α} : IsConj a b → IsConj (f a) (f b)
  | ⟨c, hc⟩ => ⟨Units.map f c, by rw [Units.coe_map, SemiconjBy, ← f.map_mul, hc.eq, f.map_mul]⟩

name: isConj_one_right
description: This theorem asserts that in a group, an element is conjugate to the identity element if and only if it is the identity element.
conditions: a is an element of a group.
conclusions: a is conjugate to the identity if and only if a = e.
function_body:
theorem isConj_one_right {a : α} : IsConj 1 a ↔ a = 1 :=
  ⟨fun ⟨c, hc⟩ => mul_right_cancel (hc.symm.trans ((mul_one _).trans (one_mul _).symm)), fun h => by
    rw [h]⟩

name: isConj_one_left
description: A tool to prove that an element is conjugate to 1 if and only if it is equal to 1 in a given type α.
conditions: Given an element a in α
Existence of an identity element 1 in α
conclusions: a is conjugate to 1 if and only if a is equal to 1
function_body:
theorem isConj_one_left {a : α} : IsConj a 1 ↔ a = 1 :=
  calc
    IsConj a 1 ↔ IsConj 1 a := ⟨IsConj.symm, IsConj.symm⟩
    _ ↔ a = 1 := isConj_one_right

name: isConj_iff
description: A theorem that provides the necessary and sufficient conditions for one element in a group to be conjugate to another.
conditions: a and b are elements of the same group
There exists an element c in the group
conclusions: a is conjugate to b if and only if there exists an element c such that c * a * c^(-1) = b
function_body:
theorem isConj_iff {a b : α} : IsConj a b ↔ ∃ c : α, c * a * c⁻¹ = b :=
  ⟨fun ⟨c, hc⟩ => ⟨c, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul.2 hc⟩, fun ⟨c, hc⟩ =>
    ⟨⟨c, c⁻¹, mul_inv_self c, inv_mul_self c⟩, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul.1 hc⟩⟩

name: conj_inv
description: This tool demonstrates that the inverse of a conjugated element equals the conjugate of the inverse element for all elements a and b in a group.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group α
function_body:
theorem conj_inv {a b : α} : (b * a * b⁻¹)⁻¹ = b * a⁻¹ * b⁻¹ :=
  ((MulAut.conj b).map_inv a).symm

name: conj_mul
description: This tool proves that the conjugation of the product of two elements is the product of the conjugations of the two elements in a group.
conditions: a, b, c are elements of a group
Each element has an inverse and the inverse operation is well-defined
conclusions: b * a * b⁻¹ * (b * c * b⁻¹) = b * (a * c) * b⁻¹
function_body:
theorem conj_mul {a b c : α} : b * a * b⁻¹ * (b * c * b⁻¹) = b * (a * c) * b⁻¹ :=
  ((MulAut.conj b).map_mul a c).symm

name: conj_pow
description: This tool verifies that for any natural number `i` and any two elements `a` and `b` of a group, the conjugation of `b` by `a` raised to the power `i` equals the conjugation of `b` raised to the power `i` by `a`.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group
function_body:
theorem conj_pow {i : ℕ} {a b : α} : (a * b * a⁻¹) ^ i = a * b ^ i * a⁻¹ := by
  induction' i with i hi
  · simp
  · simp [pow_succ, hi]

name: conj_zpow
description: This tool proves that for any elements a and b in a group, and any integer i, the expression (a * b * a⁻¹) ^ i equals a * b ^ i * a⁻¹ using induction on i.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group
conclusions: (a * b * a⁻¹) ^ i = a * b ^ i * a⁻¹
function_body:
theorem conj_zpow {i : ℤ} {a b : α} : (a * b * a⁻¹) ^ i = a * b ^ i * a⁻¹ := by
  induction' i
  · change (a * b * a⁻¹) ^ (_ : ℤ) = a * b ^ (_ : ℤ) * a⁻¹
    simp [zpow_ofNat]
  · simp [zpow_negSucc, conj_pow]
    rw [mul_assoc]

name: conj_injective
description: Proves that the function g is injective if and only if x * g * x⁻¹ is injective, utilizing the conjugation map properties.
conditions: x is an element of set α
x * g * x⁻¹ represents the conjugation of g by x
conclusions: g is injective if and only if x * g * x⁻¹ is injective
function_body:
theorem conj_injective {x : α} : Function.Injective fun g : α => x * g * x⁻¹ :=
  (MulAut.conj x).injective

name: isConj_iff₀
description: Determines if an element a is conjugate to an element b in a group with zero if and only if there exists a non-zero element c such that c⁻¹ * a * c = b.
conditions: a belongs to a group with zero
b belongs to the same group with zero
conclusions: a is conjugate to b if and only if there exists a non-zero element c such that c⁻¹ * a * c = b
function_body:
theorem isConj_iff₀ [GroupWithZero α] {a b : α} : IsConj a b ↔ ∃ c : α, c ≠ 0 ∧ c * a * c⁻¹ = b :=
  ⟨fun ⟨c, hc⟩ =>
    ⟨c, by
      rw [← Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val, Units.mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul]
      exact ⟨c.ne_zero, hc⟩⟩,
    fun ⟨c, c0, hc⟩ =>
    ⟨Units.mk0 c c0, by
      rw [SemiconjBy, ← Units.mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul, Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val, Units.val_mk0]
      exact hc⟩⟩

name: ConjClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between the equality of two conjugacy classes and the conjugacy of their representatives in a type α.
conditions: a and b are elements of a type α
Conjugacy is defined as an equivalence relation on α
conclusions: ConjClasses.mk a = ConjClasses.mk b if and only if IsConj a b
function_body:
theorem mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj {a b : α} : ConjClasses.mk a = ConjClasses.mk b ↔ IsConj a b :=
  Iff.intro Quotient.exact Quot.sound

name: ConjClasses.quotient_mk_eq_mk
description: This tool verifies that the equivalence class of an element in the context of conjugacy classes is the same as creating a new conjugacy class from that element.
conditions: a : α (a is an element in the set α)
conclusions: The equivalence class of a (⟦a⟧) is equal to ConjClasses.mk a
function_body:
theorem quotient_mk_eq_mk (a : α) : ⟦a⟧ = ConjClasses.mk a :=
  rfl

name: ConjClasses.quot_mk_eq_mk
description: This tool establishes the isomorphism between the quotient type formed by an equivalence relation and the type of conjugacy classes by showing that both are defined via the equivalence class of an element.
conditions: There exists an equivalence relation Setoid.r on a type α.
Quot gives the quotient type under the equivalence relation Setoid.r.
ConjClasses gives the type of conjugacy classes using the same equivalence relation Setoid.r.
conclusions: Quot.mk Setoid.r a is equal to ConjClasses.mk a for any element a.
function_body:
theorem quot_mk_eq_mk (a : α) : Quot.mk Setoid.r a = ConjClasses.mk a :=
  rfl

name: ConjClasses.forall_isConj
description: A tool to determine the equivalence between a predicate holding for all elements of a type and the predicate holding for all conjugacy classes of that type.
conditions: Predicate 'p' is defined for conjugacy classes of elements of type α
Type α has a well-defined notion of conjugacy classes and corresponding mk function to create these classes
conclusions: Predicate 'p' holds for all elements of type α if and only if it holds for all conjugacy classes of type α
function_body: theorem forall_isConj {p : ConjClasses α → Prop} : (∀ a, p a) ↔ ∀ a, p (ConjClasses.mk a) := Iff.intro (fun h _ => h _) fun h a => Quotient.inductionOn a h

name: ConjClasses.mk_surjective
description: The theorem states that the constructor `ConjClasses.mk α a` is surjective, meaning every element of the codomain has the form `ConjClasses.mk α a` for some `a`.
conclusions: Every element of the codomain is the image of at least one element of the domain
function_body:
theorem mk_surjective : Function.Surjective (@ConjClasses.mk α _) :=
  forall_isConj.2 fun a => ⟨a, rfl⟩

name: ConjClasses.one_eq_mk_one
description: A tool that verifies the value 1 is equal to the result of the ConjClasses.mk function with argument 1.
function_body:
theorem one_eq_mk_one : (1 : ConjClasses α) = ConjClasses.mk 1 :=
  rfl

name: ConjClasses.exists_rep
description: This tool helps to identify the existence of a representative element for any given conjugacy class in a group.
conditions: a is a conjugacy class of G
conclusions: There exists an element a0 in G such that a = [a0]
function_body:
theorem exists_rep (a : ConjClasses α) : ∃ a0 : α, ConjClasses.mk a0 = a :=
  Quot.exists_rep a

name: ConjClasses.map_surjective
description: This tool verifies the surjectivity of the function mapping conjugacy classes from one set to another via a surjective function.
conditions: f: α → β is a surjective function
conclusions: f ∘ conj: ConjClasses α → ConjClasses β is surjective
function_body: theorem map_surjective {f : α →* β} (hf : Function.Surjective f) : Function.Surjective (ConjClasses.map f) := by intro b obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := ConjClasses.mk_surjective b obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hf b exact ⟨ConjClasses.mk a, rfl⟩

name: ConjClasses.mk_injective
description: This tool shows that if two elements in a group are conjugate to one another, then they belong to the same conjugacy class.
conditions: Two elements a and b in G are conjugate to one another.
conclusions: The elements a and b have the same conjugacy class.
function_body: theorem mk_injective : Function.Injective (@ConjClasses.mk α _) := fun _ _ => (mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj.trans isConj_iff_eq).1

name: ConjClasses.mk_bijective
description: This tool proves the bijectivity of the function `mk` in the `ConjClasses` module of the standard library.
conditions: The function mk in the ConjClasses module is injective.
The function mk in the ConjClasses module is surjective.
conclusions: The function mk in the ConjClasses module is bijective.
function_body:
theorem mk_bijective : Function.Bijective (@ConjClasses.mk α _) :=
  ⟨mk_injective, mk_surjective⟩

name: mem_conjugatesOf_self
description: This tool verifies that any element of a group belongs to its own conjugacy class.
conditions: a is an element of a group
conclusions: a is in its own conjugacy class
function_body:
theorem mem_conjugatesOf_self {a : α} : a ∈ conjugatesOf a :=
  IsConj.refl _

name: IsConj.conjugatesOf_eq
description: This tool proves that the set of conjugates of two elements a and b in a given group α are equal if a and b are conjugate to each other.
function_body:
theorem IsConj.conjugatesOf_eq {a b : α} (ab : IsConj a b) : conjugatesOf a = conjugatesOf b :=
  Set.ext fun _ => ⟨fun ag => ab.symm.trans ag, fun bg => ab.trans bg⟩

name: isConj_iff_conjugatesOf_eq
description: A tool that provides a theorem stating that the set of elements that commute with an element a is equal to the set of elements that commute with its conjugate b.
conditions: a and b are conjugate elements of a group.
conclusions: The set of elements that commute with a is equal to the set of elements that commute with b.
function_body:
theorem isConj_iff_conjugatesOf_eq {a b : α} : IsConj a b ↔ conjugatesOf a = conjugatesOf b :=
  ⟨IsConj.conjugatesOf_eq, fun h => by
    have ha := @mem_conjugatesOf_self _ _ b -- Porting note: added `@`.
    rwa [← h] at ha⟩

name: ConjClasses.mem_carrier_mk
description: This tool proves that any element 'a' is a member of the carrier of its conjugacy class, leveraging the fact that any element is conjugate to itself.
conditions: a is an element of set α
conclusions: a is a member of the carrier of its conjugacy class
function_body:
theorem mem_carrier_mk {a : α} : a ∈ carrier (ConjClasses.mk a) :=
  IsConj.refl _

name: ConjClasses.mem_carrier_iff_mk_eq
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between an element being in a carrier of a conjugacy class and the equality of the conjugacy class created by the element with the given class.
function_body: theorem mem_carrier_iff_mk_eq {a : α} {b : ConjClasses α} : a ∈ carrier b ↔ ConjClasses.mk a = b := by revert b rw [forall_isConj] intro b rw [carrier, eq_comm, mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj, ← quotient_mk_eq_mk, Quotient.lift_mk] rfl

name: ConjClasses.carrier_eq_preimage_mk
description: Theorem stating that the carrier of a conjugacy class is equal to the preimage of the class under the mapping that takes an element to its conjugacy class.
conditions: a is a conjugacy class in G
function_body:
theorem carrier_eq_preimage_mk {a : ConjClasses α} : a.carrier = ConjClasses.mk ⁻¹' {a} :=
  Set.ext fun _ => mem_carrier_iff_mk_eq

name: toDual_one
description: A tool that provides a proof that the dual of the terminal object in the category of types is also the terminal object.
conditions: The category of types has a terminal object 1
conclusions: The dual of the terminal object 1 is also 1
function_body: theorem toDual_one [One α] : toDual (1 : α) = 1 := rfl

name: ofDual_one
description: This tool proves that for any type α with exactly one element, the value of the function ofDual applied to 1 is equal to 1.
conditions: α is a type with one element
function_body: theorem ofDual_one [One α] : (ofDual 1 : α) = 1 := rfl

name: toDual_mul
description: This tool verifies that in a monoid, the dual operation applied to the product of two elements equals the product of their duals.
conditions: The operation is a binary operation in a monoid.
The dual is defined as the inverse operation.
conclusions: The dual of the multiplication of two elements is equal to the multiplication of their duals.
function_body: theorem toDual_mul [Mul α] (a b : α) : toDual (a * b) = toDual a * toDual b := rfl

name: ofDual_mul
description: A theorem that states the dual of the product of two dual numbers is equal to the product of the duals of the individual dual numbers.
conditions: α is a type that supports multiplication.
a and b are elements of the dual space αᵒᵈ.
conclusions: ofDual (a * b) = ofDual a * ofDual b
function_body: theorem ofDual_mul [Mul α] (a b : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual (a * b) = ofDual a * ofDual b := rfl

name: toDual_inv
description: This tool verifies that the inverse of the dual of an element is equal to the dual of the inverse of that element.
conditions: a is an element of a group or structure that supports inverses.
function_body: theorem toDual_inv [Inv α] (a : α) : toDual a⁻¹ = (toDual a)⁻¹ := rfl

name: ofDual_inv
description: This tool demonstrates that the inverse of the dual of an involutive element is equal to the inverse of the dual of that element.
function_body: theorem ofDual_inv [Inv α] (a : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual a⁻¹ = (ofDual a)⁻¹ := rfl

name: toDual_div
description: This tool proves that the dual of the quotient a/b is equal to the quotient of the duals toDual(a) / toDual(b).
conditions: a and b must belong to a type with a division operator (Div α)
conclusions: The dual of the quotient a/b is equal to the quotient of the duals toDual(a) / toDual(b)
function_body: theorem toDual_div [Div α] (a b : α) : toDual (a / b) = toDual a / toDual b := rfl

name: ofDual_div
description: This tool verifies that the inverse of the division of two odd elements in a ring is equivalent to the division of their respective inverses.
conditions: a and b are elements of a ring
a and b are invertible (have multiplicative inverses)
conclusions: The inverse of a/b is equal to a^-1 / b^-1
function_body: theorem ofDual_div [Div α] (a b : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual (a / b) = ofDual a / ofDual b := rfl

name: toDual_pow
description: A theorem stating that for any types α and β, and any elements a : α and b : β, the equality toDual (a ^ b) = toDual a ^ b holds.
conditions: a is an element of type α
b is an element of type β
There is an instance of Pow α β
conclusions: toDual (a ^ b) is equal to toDual a ^ b
function_body: theorem toDual_pow [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : β) : toDual (a ^ b) = toDual a ^ b := rfl

name: ofDual_pow
description: A tool to prove that the dual of a power \(a^b\) is the same as the power itself, given certain conditions.
function_body: theorem ofDual_pow [Pow α β] (a : αᵒᵈ) (b : β) : ofDual (a ^ b) = ofDual a ^ b := rfl

name: pow_toDual
description: A tool that confirms the equality of the power of an element with respect to the dual of an exponent to the original power expression.
conditions: The exponent is transformed using the toDual function.
conclusions: The power operation with toDual transformed exponent is equal to the power operation with the original exponent.
function_body: theorem pow_toDual [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : β) : a ^ toDual b = a ^ b := rfl

name: pow_ofDual
description: A tool that verifies the equivalence of exponentiation operations involving an element of a type α and an element of the dual type β.
conditions: β is a dual type of α.
There exists a `Pow` typeclass instance for `α` and `β`.
conclusions: a ^ ofDual b is equal to a ^ b.
function_body: theorem pow_ofDual [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : βᵒᵈ) : a ^ ofDual b = a ^ b := rfl

name: toLex_one
description: This tool verifies that the lexical conversion of the number 1 remains 1 within the given context of type α.
conditions: α must be an instance of the type class One (α)
function_body: theorem toLex_one [One α] : toLex (1 : α) = 1 := rfl

name: ofLex_one
description: This tool proves that applying the ofLex function to the number 1 yields the element 1 in the type α.
conditions: The type α has an instance of the One typeclass
function_body: theorem ofLex_one [One α] : (ofLex 1 : α) = 1 := rfl

name: toLex_mul
description: A tool that states the comparison of the numbers a and b in multiplication is equivalent to the comparison of a and b independently.
conditions: The multiplication operation is associative and commutative.
conclusions: The comparison of a and b in the product a * b is equivalent to the comparison of a and b independently.
function_body: theorem toLex_mul [Mul α] (a b : α) : toLex (a * b) = toLex a * toLex b := rfl

name: ofLex_mul
description: A tool that demonstrates the equality of ofLex(a * b) and ofLex(a) * ofLex(b) using the Mul instance of Lex.
conditions: a and b must be instances of Lex α.
α must have a Mul instance.
conclusions: ofLex (a * b) is equal to ofLex a * ofLex b.
function_body: theorem ofLex_mul [Mul α] (a b : Lex α) : ofLex (a * b) = ofLex a * ofLex b := rfl

name: toLex_inv
description: A theorem that states the inverse of the toLex conversion of an element is equal to the toLex conversion of the inverse of that element in an ordered type.
conditions: toLex is a function that converts elements of α to lists of natural numbers representing their position in the ordering
conclusions: The inverse of toLex(a) is equal to toLex(a⁻¹)
function_body: theorem toLex_inv [Inv α] (a : α) : toLex a⁻¹ = (toLex a)⁻¹ := rfl

name: lexicographical_inverse
description: This tool verifies that the inverse permutation of a lexicographical permutation is also a lexicographical permutation.
conditions: a and its inverse a^{-1} have the same length
conclusions: The i-th element of a^{-1} is equal to the i-th element of a for all i
function_body:
theorem lexicographical_inverse [Inv α] (a : Lex α) : ofLex a⁻¹ = (ofLex a)⁻¹ := by
  assume index
  have : 
    ∀ index, a⁻¹ ! index = a ! index :=
    λ index, rfl
  exact this

name: toLex_div
description: A function that states that the lexical representation of the division of two values is equal to the division of their lexical representations.
conclusions: The lexical representation of the division of two values is equal to the division of their lexical representation.
function_body: theorem toLex_div [Div α] (a b : α) : toLex (a / b) = toLex a / toLex b := rfl

name: ofLex_div
description: This tool demonstrates the relationship between the division of elements in a lexicographically ordered set and their respective equivalents under the ofLex function.
conditions: α is a lexicographic order on set S
function_body: theorem ofLex_div [Div α] (a b : Lex α) : ofLex (a / b) = ofLex a / ofLex b := rfl

name: toLex_pow
description: This tool demonstrates that raising an element 'a' to the power 'b' in a partially ordered set (poset) is equivalent to raising the 'toLex' representation of 'a' to 'b'.
conditions: a and b are elements of a poset
function_body: theorem toLex_pow [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : β) : toLex (a ^ b) = toLex a ^ b := rfl

name: ofLex_pow
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that for Lexicographic orders α and β, the Lex order on the type α^β is given by the product Lex order.
conclusions: The Lex order on α^β is the product Lex order
function_body: theorem ofLex_pow [Pow α β] (a : Lex α) (b : β) : ofLex (a ^ b) = ofLex a ^ b := rfl

name: pow_toLex
description: This tool verifies that raising a number 'a' to the power of 'b' results in 'a' raised to the power of 'b', as defined by the repeated multiplication of 'a' by itself 'b' times.
conditions: a is a member of set α
b is a member of set β
The power operation is defined for elements of α and β
conclusions: a raised to the power of b equals a raised to the power of b
function_body: theorem pow_toLex [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : β) : a ^ toLex b = a ^ b := rfl

name: pow_ofLex
description: This tool verifies that a power of a tuple is equal to the power of each component of the tuple.
conditions: α is a type with a power operation
β is a type with a power operation
Lex β is a lexical ordering of β
conclusions: The power of a tuple (a, b) is equal to the power of each component, i.e., a^ofLex(b) = a^b.
function_body: theorem pow_ofLex [Pow α β] (a : α) (b : Lex β) : a ^ ofLex b = a ^ b := rfl

name: Monoid.ext
description: This tool proves that two monoids are equal if their multiplication operations are equal.
conditions: m₁ and m₂ are Monoids on M
function_body:
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) : m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (this)
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

name: CommMonoid.toMonoid_injective
description: A theorem that proves the injectivity of the function embedding a commutative monoid into monoids.
conditions: M is an arbitrary commutative monoid
Two embeddings of commutative monoids are given
conclusions: The two embeddings must be equal at the underlying elements
function_body:
theorem CommMonoid.toMonoid_injective {M : Type u} :
    Function.Injective (@CommMonoid.toMonoid M) := by
  rintro ⟨⟩ ⟨⟩ h
  congr

name: CommMonoid.ext
description: A theorem that asserts the equality of two elements in a commutative monoid if their product commutes.
conditions: m1 and m2 are elements of M
function_body:
theorem CommMonoid.ext {M : Type*} ⦃m₁ m₂ : CommMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) : m₁ = m₂ :=
  CommMonoid.toMonoid_injective <| Monoid.ext h_mul

name: LeftCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective
description: This tool verifies the injectivity of the function that maps elements of a left cancellative monoid to their respective equivalence classes in the constructed monoid.
conditions: M is a left cancellative monoid
conclusions: The function that maps elements of M to their equivalence classes in the monoid constructed from M is injective
function_body:
theorem LeftCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective {M : Type u} :
Function.Injective (@LeftCancelMonoid.toMonoid M) := by

name: LeftCancelMonoid.ext
description: A tool that proves the equivalence of two LeftCancelMonoids based on their multiplication operation.
conditions: m1 and m2 have the same multiplication operation
function_body:
theorem LeftCancelMonoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : LeftCancelMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) : m₁ = m₂ :=
  LeftCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective <| Monoid.ext h_mul

name: RightCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective
description: This tool proves the injectivity of the function `toMonoid` in the context of a right cancel monoid. It demonstrates that two elements of a right cancel monoid mapping to the same element in the associated monoid must be equal.
conditions: M is a right cancel monoid
toMonoid x = toMonoid y for elements x and y
function_body:
theorem RightCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective {M : Type u} : Function.Injective (@RightCancelMonoid.toMonoid M) := by

name: RightCancelMonoid.ext
description: This theorem demonstrates that in a RightCancelMonoid, if two elements have the same product, then the elements are equal.
conditions: m₁ and m₂ are elements of a RightCancelMonoid
m₁ and m₂ have the same product
function_body:
theorem RightCancelMonoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : RightCancelMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) : m₁ = m₂ :=
  RightCancelMonoid.toMonoid_injective <| Monoid.ext h_mul

name: CancelMonoid.toLeftCancelMonoid_injective
description: A theorem stating that the function CancelMonoid.toLeftCancelMonoid is injective for any type M.
function_body:
theorem CancelMonoid.toLeftCancelMonoid_injective {M : Type u} :
    Function.Injective (@CancelMonoid.toLeftCancelMonoid M) := by
