name: CancelMonoid.ext
description: A tool to prove that two cancel monoids with the same multiplication operation are equal.
conditions: Two cancel monoids m₁ and m₂
The multiplication operation of m₁ is equal to the multiplication operation of m₂
conclusions: The two cancel monoids m₁ and m₂ are equal
function_body:
theorem CancelMonoid.ext {M : Type*} ⦃m₁ m₂ : CancelMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) :
    m₁ = m₂ :=
  CancelMonoid.toLeftCancelMonoid_injective <| LeftCancelMonoid.ext h_mul

name: CancelCommMonoid.toCommMonoid_injective
description: This theorem proves that the function `toCommMonoid` from a cancellation commutative monoid to a commutative monoid is injective.
conditions: M is a cancellation commutative monoid
x and y are elements of M

name: CancelCommMonoid.ext
description: This tool provides a theorem that if the multiplication functions of two elements in a CancelCommMonoid are equal, then the elements themselves are equal.
conditions: m₁ and m₂ are elements of CancelCommMonoid M
function_body:
theorem CancelCommMonoid.ext {M : Type*} ⦃m₁ m₂ : CancelCommMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) : m₁ = m₂ :=
  CancelCommMonoid.toCommMonoid_injective <| CommMonoid.ext h_mul

name: DivInvMonoid.ext
description: A tool to determine the equality of two elements in a type equipped with a division and inverse operation, given that they have the same multiplication and inverse operations.
conditions: M is a type equipped with division and inverse operations.
m₁ and m₂ are two elements of M such that m₁.mul = m₂.mul.
m₁ and m₂ have the same inverse operations, i.e., m₁.inv = m₂.inv.
function_body:
theorem DivInvMonoid.ext {M : Type*} ⦃m₁ m₂ : DivInvMonoid M⦄ (h_mul : m₁.mul = m₂.mul) (h_inv : m₁.inv = m₂.inv) : m₁ = m₂ := by
  have h_mon := Monoid.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) h_mon
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := congr_arg (·.npow) h_mon
  have : m₁.zpow = m₂.zpow := by
    ext m x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_zpow' M M m₁ m₂ f (congr_fun h_inv) x m
  have : m₁.div = m₂.div := by
    ext a b
    exact @map_div' _ _
      (@MonoidHom _ _ (_) _) (id _) _
      (@MonoidHom.monoidHomClass _ _ (_) _) f (congr_fun h_inv) a b
  rcases m₁ with @⟨_, ⟨_⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨_, ⟨_⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

name: Group.ext
description: A theorem tool that proves two elements in a group are equal if their product with another element commutes.
conditions: g1 and g2 are elements of G.
function_body:
theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : G⦄ (h_mul : g₁ * g₂ = g₂ * g₁) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  showTheorem
  have h₁ : g₁ * 1 = g₂ * 1 := by rw [h_mul]; rfl
  suffices h₂ : ∀ x, g₁ * x = g₂ * x
  let f : G →* G := by refine_struct { toFun := fun x ↦ g₁ * x * g₁⁻¹ }
  exact function.Injective
  let x₀ := x * (g₁⁻¹ * g₂) * g₁
  specialize h₂ (g₁⁻¹ * g₂)
  simp only [h₂, one_mul, mul_inv_rev, mul_right_inj] at h₁ ⊢
  rw [one_mul] at h₂
  choose x₁ using λ _ ↦ g₁⁻¹ * g₂ * g₁⁻¹
  exact function.surjective
  rw [←h_mul, mul_assoc]
  show equality
  set Equality : (g₁ ^ g₁⁻¹) == g₂ with h_main
  rwa h_mul

name: CommGroup.ext
description: This tool proves that in a commutative group, two elements that have the same product are equal.
function_body:
theorem CommGroup.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : CommGroup G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ :=
  CommGroup.toGroup_injective <| Group.ext h_mul

name: pow_ite
description: A tool that encapsulates the theorem proving that if a value is raised to a power determined by a conditional expression, it equals the appropriate power based on the condition.
conditions: The existence of a decidable proposition P
The presence of two exponents 'b' and 'c'
conclusions: The expression a^(if P then b else c) equals to if P then a^b else a^c
function_body: theorem pow_ite (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (a : M) (b c : ℕ) : (a ^ if P then b else c) = if P then a ^ b else a ^ c := by split_ifs <;> rfl

name: ite_pow
description: A tool that provides a proof showing the equality $(a + b)^c = a^c + b^c$ for all elements \(a, b\) in a monoid \(M\) and \(c\) in the natural numbers.
conditions: a, b are elements of a monoid M
function_body: theorem ite_pow (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (a b : M) (c : ℕ) : (if P then a else b) ^ c = if P then a ^ c else b ^ c := by split_ifs <;> rfl

name: nsmul_zero
description: This tool proves that the product of any natural number and zero is always zero. The proof uses mathematical induction on the natural number.
function_body:
theorem nsmul_zero (n : ℕ) : n • (0 : A) = 0 := by
  induction' n with n ih
  · exact zero_nsmul _
  · rw [succ_nsmul, ih, add_zero]

name: one_nsmul
description: This tool proves that multiplying an integer by 1 yields the integer itself.
function_body: theorem one_nsmul (a : A) : 1 • a = a := by rw [succ_nsmul, zero_nsmul, add_zero]

name: add_nsmul
description: This theorem states that for any element a in an additive monoid A and natural numbers m and n, the n-fold addition of m and n applied to a equals the sum of the n-fold additions of m and n individually applied to a.
conditions: a is an element of the additive monoid A
m and n are natural numbers
conclusions: (m + n) • a = m • a + n • a
function_body:
theorem add_nsmul (a : A) (m n : ℕ) : (m + n) • a = m • a + n • a := by
  induction m with
  | zero => rw [Nat.zero_add, zero_nsmul, zero_add]
  | succ m ih => rw [Nat.succ_add, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, succ_nsmul, ih, succ_nsmul, add_assoc]

name: one_pow
description: This tool proves that for any natural number n, raising 1 to the power n equals 1. This is done using the principle of mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem one_pow (n : ℕ) : (1 : M) ^ n = 1 := by
  induction' n with n ih
  · exact pow_zero _
  · rw [pow_succ, ih, one_mul]

name: pow_one
description: This tool proves that for any matrix A, raising A to the power of 1 results in A.
function_body: theorem pow_one (a : M) : a ^ 1 = a := by rw [pow_succ, pow_zero, mul_one]

name: pow_two
description: A tool that provides the multiplication equivalence of squaring an element in a given mathematical structure.
conditions: a is an element of a multiplicative monoid M
M is a structure where the power operation (^) and multiplication (*) are defined, along with the identity element 1
function_body: theorem pow_two (a : M) : a ^ 2 = a * a := by rw [pow_succ, pow_one]

name: pow_three'
description: This tool demonstrates and proves the formula for raising a number 'a' to the power of 3, resulting in the expression a * a * a.
conditions: 'a' must be an element of a mathematical structure that supports multiplication and exponentiation.
conclusions: The formula for 'a ^ 3' is 'a * a * a'
function_body: theorem pow_three' (a : M) : a ^ 3 = a * a * a := by rw [pow_succ', pow_two]

name: pow_three
description: This tool provides a theorem for any element in a monoid, proving that the cube of an element is equal to the element multiplied by its square.
conditions: a is an element of M
function_body: theorem pow_three (a : M) : a ^ 3 = a * (a * a) := by rw [pow_succ, pow_two]

name: pow_add
description: This tool verifies that for any element a in a magma M and any natural numbers m and n, the equation a^(m + n) = a^m * a^n holds true.
conditions: a is an element of a magma M
m and n are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem pow_add (a : M) (m n : ℕ) : a ^ (m + n) = a ^ m * a ^ n := by
  induction' n with n ih
  · rw [Nat.add_zero, pow_zero, mul_one]
  · rw [pow_succ', ← mul_assoc, ← ih, ← pow_succ', Nat.add_assoc]

name: pow_mul'
description: This tool proves that for any element a in a monoid M and any natural numbers m and n, the expression a raised to the product of m and n equals the m-th power of a raised to the n-th power.
conditions: a is an element of a monoid M
function_body: theorem pow_mul' (a : M) (m n : ℕ) : a ^ (m * n) = (a ^ n) ^ m := by rw [Nat.mul_comm, pow_mul]

name: Commute.mul_pow
description: This theorem states that if two elements a and b of a monoid commute, then the nth power of their product equals the product of their nth powers.
conditions: a and b are elements of a monoid M
conclusions: (ab)^n = a^n b^n for all natural numbers n
function_body:
theorem Commute.mul_pow {a b : M} (h : Commute a b) (n : ℕ) : (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n := by
  induction' n with n ih
  · rw [pow_zero, pow_zero, pow_zero, one_mul]
  · simp only [pow_succ, ih, ← mul_assoc, (h.pow_left n).right_comm]

name: pow_mul_comm'
description: A tool that demonstrates the commutativity of exponentiation followed by multiplication in a magma.
conditions: a is an element of M.
conclusions: a ^ n * a = a * a ^ n in magma M.
function_body:
theorem pow_mul_comm' (a : M) (n : ℕ) : a ^ n * a = a * a ^ n :=
  Commute.pow_self a n

name: pow_boole
description: Proves that a^1 = a when P is true, and a^0 = 1 when P is false.
conclusions: a^(if P then 1 else 0) = if P then a else 1
function_body: theorem pow_boole (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (a : M) : (a ^ if P then 1 else 0) = if P then a else 1 := by simp

name: pow_right_comm
description: This theorem states that for any element in a monoid and any natural numbers, exponentiation is commutative when applied in a nested fashion.
conditions: a is an element of M
m and n are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem pow_right_comm (a : M) (m n : ℕ) : (a ^ m) ^ n = (a ^ n) ^ m := by
  rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm, pow_mul]

name: pow_mul_pow_sub
description: This tool proves that for any natural numbers m and n where m is less than or equal to n, and for any element a of a monoid, a^m multiplied by a^(n - m) is equal to a^n.
conditions: m and n are natural numbers
a is an element of a monoid M
function_body:
theorem pow_mul_pow_sub (a : M) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : a ^ m * a ^ (n - m) = a ^ n := by
  rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_comm, Nat.sub_add_cancel h]

name: pow_sub_mul_pow
description: This tool proves that for any element 'a' in a monoid 'M', and for any natural numbers 'm' and 'n' where 'm ≤ n', the equation a^(n - m) * a^m equals a^n.
conditions: m and n are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem pow_sub_mul_pow (a : M) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : a ^ (n - m) * a ^ m = a ^ n := by
  rw [← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel h]

name: pow_eq_pow_mod
description: This theorem shows that in a monoid, if an element x raised to the power of n equals 1, then x raised to the power of any positive integer m is equal to x raised to m modulo n.
conditions: x is an element of M
x raised to the power of n equals 1
conclusions: x raised to the power of m equals x raised to m modulo n for any positive integer m
function_body:
theorem pow_eq_pow_mod {M : Type*} [Monoid M] {x : M} (m : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (h : x ^ n = 1) :
    x ^ m = x ^ (m % n) := by
  have t : x ^ m = x ^ (n * (m / n) + m % n) :=
    congr_arg (fun a => x ^ a) ((Nat.add_comm _ _).trans (Nat.mod_add_div _ _)).symm
  rw [t, pow_add, pow_mul, h, one_pow, one_mul]

name: pow_mul_comm
description: A theorem that states the commutative property for exponentiation, where the order of multiplication for exponentiated terms does not affect the result.
conditions: a is an element of a commutative monoid M
m and n are natural numbers
conclusions: a ^ m * a ^ n = a ^ n * a ^ m
function_body:
theorem pow_mul_comm (a : M) (m n : ℕ) : a ^ m * a ^ n = a ^ n * a ^ m :=
  Commute.pow_pow_self a m n

name: pow_bit0
description: Proves that for any element a in a monoid M, raising a to bit0 n is equivalent to multiplying a^n by itself.
conditions: a is an element of a monoid M
function_body:
theorem pow_bit0 (a : M) (n : ℕ) : a ^ bit0 n = a ^ n * a ^ n :=
pow_add _ _ _

name: pow_bit1
description: This theorem states that raising an element 'a' to the power of 'bit1 n' is equivalent to multiplying 'a' raised to the power of 'n' by itself and then by 'a'.
conditions: a is an element of a monoid M
n is a natural number ℕ
conclusions: a ^ bit1 n = a ^ n * a ^ n * a
function_body:
theorem pow_bit1 (a : M) (n : ℕ) : a ^ bit1 n = a ^ n * a ^ n * a := by
  rw [bit1, pow_succ', pow_bit0]

name: pow_bit1'
description: Proves that for any element a in a monoid M and any natural number n, a^bit1 n = (a^2)^n * a.
conditions: a is an element of a monoid M
conclusions: a ^ bit1 n = (a * a) ^ n * a
function_body:
theorem pow_bit1' (a : M) (n : ℕ) : a ^ bit1 n = (a * a) ^ n * a := by
  rw [bit1, pow_succ', pow_bit0']

name: pow_mul_pow_eq_one
description: This tool proves that given two elements a and b in a multiplicative monoid M such that their product is 1, the product of their nth powers is also 1 for any natural number n.
function_body:
theorem pow_mul_pow_eq_one {a b : M} (n : ℕ) (h : a * b = 1) : a ^ n * b ^ n = 1 := by
  induction' n with n hn
  · simp
  · calc
      a ^ n.succ * b ^ n.succ = a ^ n * a * (b * b ^ n) := by rw [pow_succ', pow_succ]
      _ = a ^ n * (a * b) * b ^ n := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = 1 := by simp [h, hn]

name: dvd_pow
description: A tool that proves if an integer x divides another integer y, then x also divides any positive power of y.
function_body:
theorem dvd_pow {x y : M} (hxy : x ∣ y) : ∀ {n : ℕ} (_ : n ≠ 0), x ∣ y ^ n
  | 0,     hn => (hn rfl).elim
  | n + 1, _  => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact hxy.mul_right _

name: dvd_pow_self
description: This tool states that if a number 'a' divides another number 'b', then 'a' also divides 'b' raised to any positive integer power.
conclusions: a divides b^n for all positive integers n
function_body:
theorem dvd_pow_self (a : M) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ∣ a ^ n :=
  dvd_rfl.pow hn

name: mul_pow
description: A theorem that shows that for any two elements 'a' and 'b' in a monoid 'M' and a natural number 'n', the power of their product is equal to the product of their individual powers.
conditions: a and b are elements of a monoid M
Multiplication in the monoid is associative
function_body:
theorem mul_pow (a b : M) (n : ℕ) : (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n :=
  (Commute.all a b).mul_pow n

name: zpow_one
description: This tool verifies that raising any element 'a' of group 'G' to the power of 1 results in 'a' itself in the context of integer exponentiation.
conditions: a is an element of group G
function_body:
theorem zpow_one (a : G) : a ^ (1 : ℤ) = a := by
  convert pow_one a using 1
  exact zpow_ofNat a 1

name: zpow_two
description: A tool that proves the statement a^2 = a * a for any group element a by defining exponentiation in terms of the group's multiplication operation.
conditions: a is an element of a group G
conclusions: a^2 = a * a for any group element a
function_body:
theorem zpow_two (a : G) : a ^ (2 : ℤ) = a * a := by
  convert pow_two a using 1
  exact zpow_ofNat a 2

name: zpow_neg_one
description: This theorem states that for any element x in a group G, raising x to the power of negative one is equivalent to taking the inverse of x.
conditions: x is an element of a group G
conclusions: x^(-1) is equal to x's inverse
function_body:
theorem zpow_neg_one (x : G) : x ^ (-1 : ℤ) = x⁻¹ :=
  (zpow_negSucc x 0).trans <| congr_arg Inv.inv (pow_one x)

name: zpow_neg_coe_of_pos
description: This theorem states that for any group element a and any positive integer n, the negative nth power of a is equal to the inverse of the nth power of a.
conditions: a is an element of a group G
function_body:
theorem zpow_neg_coe_of_pos (a : G) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → a ^ (-(n : ℤ)) = (a ^ n)⁻¹
  | _ + 1, _ => zpow_negSucc _ _

name: inv_pow
description: This tool provides the inverse of \\(a^n\\) in terms of \\(a^{-1}\\) and proves that the expression \\((a^n)^{-1} = (a^{-1})^n\\).
conditions: a is a non-zero element within a multiplicative group or field
n is a non-negative integer (n ∈ ℕ)
function_body:
theorem inv_pow (a : α) : ∀ n : ℕ, a⁻¹ ^ n = (a ^ n)⁻¹
  | 0 => by rw [pow_zero, pow_zero, inv_one]
  | n + 1 => by rw [pow_succ', pow_succ, inv_pow _ n, mul_inv_rev]

name: one_zpow
description: This tool proves that 1 raised to any power (whether positive, zero, or negative) is always equal to 1 for all integers n.
function_body:
theorem one_zpow : ∀ n : ℤ, (1 : α) ^ n = 1
  | (n : ℕ)       => by rw [zpow_ofNat, one_pow]
  | .negSucc n => by rw [zpow_negSucc, one_pow, inv_one]

name: zpow_neg
description: This tool provides the functionality to compute a^(-n) as the inverse of a^n for any element a in an additive group with involution and any integer n.
conditions: a is an element of an additive group with involution
function_body:
theorem zpow_neg (a : α) : ∀ n : ℤ, a ^ (-n) = (a ^ n)⁻¹
  | (n + 1 : ℕ) => DivInvMonoid.zpow_neg' _ _
  | 0 => by
    change a ^ (0 : ℤ) = (a ^ (0 : ℤ))⁻¹
    simp
  | Int.negSucc n => by
    rw [zpow_negSucc, inv_inv, ← zpow_ofNat]
    rfl

name: mul_zpow_neg_one
description: This tool demonstrates that the inverse of a product in a group is the product of the inverses in reverse order.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group α
Group α must support exponentiation with integers, particularly with -1
function_body:
theorem mul_zpow_neg_one (a b : α) : (a * b) ^ (-1 : ℤ) = b ^ (-1 : ℤ) * a ^ (-1 : ℤ) := by
  simp only [zpow_neg, zpow_one, mul_inv_rev]

name: inv_zpow
description: This tool proves that for any element \(a\) and any integer \(n\), the inverse of \(a^n\) equals \(a^{-1}\) raised to the nth power.
conditions: a is an element of a group with a defined inverse
function_body:
theorem inv_zpow (a : α) : ∀ n : ℤ, a⁻¹ ^ n = (a ^ n)⁻¹
  | (n : ℕ)    => by rw [zpow_ofNat, zpow_ofNat, inv_pow]
  | .negSucc n => by rw [zpow_negSucc, zpow_negSucc, inv_pow]

name: inv_zpow'
description: A theorem that proves for any element `a` of an abelian group and any integer `n`, the equation `a^(-n) = (a^-1)^n` holds.
conditions: a is an element of an abelian group
function_body: theorem inv_zpow' (a : α) (n : ℤ) : a⁻¹ ^ n = a ^ (-n) := by rw [inv_zpow, zpow_neg]

name: one_div_pow
description: This tool asserts that for any non-zero element a in a ring and any positive integer n, the result of raising (1/a) to the power of n is equal to 1 divided by a raised to the power of n.
conditions: a is a non-zero element in a ring
function_body: theorem one_div_pow (a : α) (n : ℕ) : (1 / a) ^ n = 1 / a ^ n := by simp only [one_div, inv_pow]

name: one_div_zpow
description: Proves that raising the reciprocal of a number to an integer power is the same as taking the reciprocal of the number raised to that power.
conditions: a is a nonzero element of a field α
function_body: theorem one_div_zpow (a : α) (n : ℤ) : (1 / a) ^ n = 1 / a ^ n := by simp only [one_div, inv_zpow]

name: Commute.mul_zpow
description: This tool proves that for any two commuting elements `a` and `b`, the exponentiation of their product equals the product of their individual exponentiations for all integers `i`.
conditions: Elements a and b must commute
conclusions: (a * b) ^ i = a ^ i * b ^ i for all i in ℤ
function_body:
theorem Commute.mul_zpow (h : Commute a b) : ∀ i : ℤ, (a * b) ^ i = a ^ i * b ^ i
  | (n : ℕ)    => by simp [zpow_ofNat, h.mul_pow n]
  | .negSucc n => by simp [h.mul_pow, (h.pow_pow _ _).eq, mul_inv_rev]

name: mul_zpow
description: A theorem that proves for any two numbers a and b, the expression (a * b) raised to the power of n equals a^n multiplied by b^n.
function_body:
theorem mul_zpow (a b : α) : ∀ n : ℤ, (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n :=
  (Commute.all a b).mul_zpow

name: div_pow
description: This tool proves that raising a quotient to a natural number power is equivalent to raising the numerator and denominator to that power separately.
conditions: a and b are elements of a ring.
The ring must support division, which implies that 1/b makes sense.
conclusions: (a / b) ^ n = a ^ n / b ^ n
function_body:
theorem div_pow (a b : α) (n : ℕ) : (a / b) ^ n = a ^ n / b ^ n := by
  simp only [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_pow, inv_pow]

name: div_zpow
description: This theorem verifies that for numbers a and b, and an integer n, the power of their quotient is equivalent to the quotient of their respective powers.
conclusions: (a / b) ^ n = a ^ n / b ^ n
function_body:
theorem div_zpow (a b : α) (n : ℤ) : (a / b) ^ n = a ^ n / b ^ n := by
  simp only [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_zpow, inv_zpow]

name: pow_inv_comm
description: This theorem states that for any element a in a group G, and for all natural numbers m and n, the product of the m-th power of the inverse of a and the n-th power of a is equal to the product of the n-th power of a and the m-th power of the inverse of a.
conditions: a is an element of a group G
conclusions: a⁻¹ ^ m * a ^ n = a ^ n * a⁻¹ ^ m
function_body:
theorem pow_inv_comm (a : G) (m n : ℕ) : a⁻¹ ^ m * a ^ n = a ^ n * a⁻¹ ^ m :=
  (Commute.refl a).inv_left.pow_pow _ _

name: inv_pow_sub
description: Given an element a in a group G and natural numbers m, n with n <= m, this tool proves that a^-1^(m-n) = (a^m)^-1 * a^n.
conditions: a is an element of group G
m and n are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem inv_pow_sub (a : G) {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) : a⁻¹ ^ (m - n) = (a ^ m)⁻¹ * a ^ n := by
  rw [pow_sub a⁻¹ h, inv_pow, inv_pow, inv_inv]

name: pow_dvd_pow
description: This tool verifies if one power of an element divides another power of the same element given certain conditions in a monoid.
function_body:
theorem pow_dvd_pow [Monoid R] (a : R) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : a ^ m ∣ a ^ n :=
  ⟨a ^ (n - m), by rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_comm, Nat.sub_add_cancel h]⟩

name: ofAdd_nsmul
description: This tool proves that for any element x in an additive monoid A and any natural number n, the multiplicative inverse of the additive multiple n • x is equal to the multiplicative inverse of x raised to the power n.
conditions: x is an element in an additive monoid A
conclusions: Multiplicative inverse of n • x is equal to the multiplicative inverse of x raised to the power n
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_nsmul [AddMonoid A] (x : A) (n : ℕ) :
Multiplicative.ofAdd (n • x) = Multiplicative.ofAdd x ^ n :=
rfl

name: ofAdd_zsmul
description: This tool shows that the multiplicative version of the additive scaling of x by any integer n is equivalent to x raised to the power of n.
conditions: x is an element of a type A that forms a SubNegMonoid
conclusions: The multiplicative version of scaling x by n equals x raised to the power n
function_body: theorem ofAdd_zsmul [SubNegMonoid A] (x : A) (n : ℤ) : Multiplicative.ofAdd (n • x) = Multiplicative.ofAdd x ^ n := rfl

name: ofMul_pow
description: This tool provides a proof that for any monoid A and element x of A, Additive.ofMul (x ^ n) is equal to n • Additive.ofMul x.
conditions: x is an element of A
function_body: theorem ofMul_pow [Monoid A] (x : A) (n : ℕ) : Additive.ofMul (x ^ n) = n • Additive.ofMul x := rfl

name: ofMul_zpow
description: This tool shows that for any element x of a group G and any integer n, the additive inverse of x^n is n times the additive inverse of x.
conditions: x is an element of a group G
conclusions: The additive inverse of x^n is n times the additive inverse of x
function_body:
theorem ofMul_zpow [DivInvMonoid G] (x : G) (n : ℤ) :
    Additive.ofMul (x ^ n) = n • Additive.ofMul x :=
  rfl

name: SemiconjBy.zpow_right
description: A theorem that demonstrates for a group G, if a times x equals y, then for any integer m, a times x raised to the power of m equals y raised to the power of m.
conditions: a, x, y are elements of G.
conclusions: For any integer m, a times x^m equals y^m.
function_body:
theorem SemiconjBy.zpow_right [Group G] {a x y : G} (h : SemiconjBy a x y) : ∀ m : ℤ, SemiconjBy a (x ^ m) (y ^ m)
  | (n : ℕ)    => by simp [zpow_ofNat, h.pow_right n]
  | .negSucc n => by
    simp only [zpow_negSucc, inv_right_iff]
    apply pow_right h

name: Commute.zpow_right
description: Given two integers a and b that commute, this tool shows that a also commutes with b raised to any integer power m.
conditions: a and b commute (i.e., ab = ba)
conclusions: a commutes with b^m for any integer m
function_body:
theorem zpow_right (h : Commute a b) (m : ℤ) : Commute a (b ^ m) :=
  SemiconjBy.zpow_right h m

name: is_divisible_of_mul_divisible
description: Proves that for integers a, b, and c, if c divides the product of a and b, then c divides a or c divides b.
conditions: c divides the product of a and b
conclusions: c divides a or c divides b
function_body:
lemma is_divisible_of_mul_divisible (a b c : ℤ) : c ∣ a * b → c ∣ a ∨ c ∣ b :=
by
  cases h : c ∣ a * b with
  | inl ha =>
    cases h' : c ∣ a with
    | inl hca => left hca
    | inr hnac =>
      have : c = 0,
      { apply nat.eq_zero_of_dvd_zero,
        exact (nat.mul_dvd_of_dvd_right (nat.cast_of_pos hnac.pos) h) },
      have : a * b = 0,
      { apply nat.mul_eq_zero,
        exact h },
      have : b = 0,
      { rw [this, nat.cast_of_pos hnac.pos, nat.mul_zero],
        exact h },
      exact hnab
  | inr hnb => right hnb

name: Commute.zpow_zpow
description: A tool that states if two elements a and b commute, then their integral powers a^m and b^n also commute.
conclusions: a^m commutes with b^n for all integers m and n
function_body:
theorem zpow_zpow (h : Commute a b) (m n : ℤ) : Commute (a ^ m) (b ^ n) :=
  (h.zpow_left m).zpow_right n

name: Commute.self_zpow
description: This tool demonstrates that any element 'a' commutes with its own power 'a^n' in the context of group or ring theory.
conditions: a is an element of a group or ring
function_body:
theorem self_zpow : Commute a (a ^ n) :=
  (Commute.refl a).zpow_right n

name: Commute.zpow_self
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that for any number a and any positive integer n, the operation of raising a to the power of n commutes with the operation of multiplying by a.
function_body:
theorem zpow_self : Commute (a ^ n) a :=
  (Commute.refl a).zpow_left n

name: Commute.zpow_zpow_self
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that for any integer exponents m and n, the power of a number raised to another power is equivalent to the number raised to the product of the exponents.
function_body:
theorem zpow_zpow_self : Commute (a ^ m) (a ^ n) :=
  (Commute.refl a).zpow_zpow m n

name: Additive.ofMul_symm_eq
description: This tool proves that the inverse of the toMul function is the ofMul function, meaning they are equal.
conditions: The function ofMul is defined as the inverse of toMul
conclusions: The inverse of the toMul function is the ofMul function
function_body:
theorem ofMul_symm_eq : (@ofMul α).symm = toMul :=
  rfl

name: Additive.toMul_symm_eq
description: This tool demonstrates that the symmetry of the toMul function is equal to the ofMul function, indicating that their operations are reflections or inverses of each other.
conditions: The toMul function must be defined.
The inverse (symmetry) of the toMul function must be considered.
The ofMul function (multiplication of two elements) must be defined.
conclusions: The inverse (symmetry) of the toMul function is equal to the ofMul function.
function_body:
theorem toMul_symm_eq : (@toMul α).symm = ofMul :=
  rfl

name: Multiplicative.ofAdd_symm_eq
description: This theorem states that the symmetrical version of the ofAdd function is equal to the toAdd function in the context of multiplicative structures.
conditions: α is a given context where ofAdd and toAdd are defined
conclusions: The symmetrical version of ofAdd is equal to toAdd
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_symm_eq : (@ofAdd α).symm = toAdd :=
  rfl

name: LineEquationThroughPoint
description: This tool computes the equation of a line parallel to a given line that passes through a specific point.
conditions: The equation of the original line (y = mx + c), in this case y = 2x + 1.
The coordinates of the point through which the new parallel line should pass (in this case, the point (3, 5)).
conclusions: The equation of the new parallel line, in this case y = 2x - 1.
function_body: theorem LineEquationThroughPoint : For a line parallel to y = 2x + 1 passing through the point (3, 5), the equation is y = 2x - 1.

name: toAdd_ofAdd
description: A tool that verifies the conversion between additive and multiplicative representations of an element, ensuring that converting back and forth results in the original element.
conditions: x is an element of type α
function_body: theorem toAdd_ofAdd (x : α) : toAdd (ofAdd x) = x := rfl

name: ofAdd_toAdd
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem showing that applying `toAdd` and then `ofAdd` to a multiplicative value results in the original multiplicative value.
conditions: x is of type Multiplicative α
function_body: theorem ofAdd_toAdd (x : Multiplicative α) : ofAdd (toAdd x) = x := rfl

name: toMul_ofMul
description: This tool demonstrates that for any value x of type α, the function toMul applied to ofMul of x equals x, leveraging the fact that toMul and ofMul are inverse functions.
conditions: ofMul and toMul are inverse functions
function_body:
theorem toMul_ofMul (x : α) : toMul (ofMul x) = x :=
  rfl

name: ofMul_toMul
description: A proof that converting an additive element to a multiplicative element and back to an additive element yields the identity function.
conditions: x is an element of the Additive structure
function_body:
theorem ofMul_toMul (x : Additive α) : ofMul (toMul x) = x :=
  rfl

name: ofAdd_add
description: This tool demonstrates that for an additive group α, the exponential map of the group is closed under multiplication.
conclusions: The multiplicative group derived from α via the exponential map is closed under multiplication
function_body: theorem ofAdd_add [Add α] (x y : α) : ofAdd (x + y) = ofAdd x * ofAdd y := rfl

name: toAdd_mul
description: This tool proves that the additive transformation of the product of two elements equals the sum of their respective additive transformations.
conditions: x and y are elements of a multiplicative monoid
toAdd is a function that converts multiplicative structure to additive
function_body: theorem toAdd_mul [Add α] (x y : Multiplicative α) : toAdd (x * y) = toAdd x + toAdd y := rfl

name: ofMul_mul
description: This tool proves that ofMul is a homomorphism of monoids for a given multiplicative monoid.
conditions: x and y are elements of α
function_body: theorem ofMul_mul [Mul α] (x y : α) : ofMul (x * y) = ofMul x + ofMul y := rfl

name: toMul_add
description: A tool to convert the sum of two additive numbers to the product of their corresponding multiplicative numbers.
conditions: x and y are additive numbers
conclusions: toMul(x + y) is equal to toMul(x) * toMul(y)
function_body: theorem toMul_add [Mul α] (x y : Additive α) : toMul (x + y) = toMul x * toMul y := rfl

name: ofMul_one
description: A theorem stating that in an additive monoid, the additive identity with respect to multiplication by one is zero.
conditions: a is an element of an additive monoid.
function_body: theorem ofMul_one [One α] : @Additive.ofMul α 1 = 0 := rfl

name: ofMul_eq_zero
description: This theorem states that in a commutative ring with unity, an element x is equal to 1 if and only if x is a zero divisor.
conditions: x is an element of a commutative ring with unity
conclusions: x is equal to 1 if and only if x is a zero divisor
function_body: theorem ofMul_eq_zero {A : Type*} [One A] {x : A} : Additive.ofMul x = 0 ↔ x = 1 := Iff.rfl

name: toMul_zero
description: This theorem asserts that the multiplicative inverse of the additive identity (0) in an algebraic structure with a multiplicative identity (1) is 1.
conditions: The structure has a multiplicative identity (1).
0 is the additive identity in the given structure.
function_body: theorem toMul_zero [One α] : toMul (0 : Additive α) = 1 := rfl

name: ofAdd_zero
description: This tool verifies that if 0 is the additive identity in an additive group, then it is the multiplicative identity in the corresponding multiplicative group.
conditions: 0 is the additive identity in the additive group (A, +).
conclusions: 0 is the multiplicative identity in the corresponding multiplicative group (A^×, ·).
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_zero [Zero α] : @Multiplicative.ofAdd α 0 = 1 :=
  rfl

name: ofAdd_eq_one
description: This tool provides a proof that for any type A with an additive monoid structure, the equivalence A × → 1 equals A × 0.
conditions: A is a type with an additive monoid structure
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_eq_one {A : Type*} [Zero A] {x : A} : Multiplicative.ofAdd x = 1 ↔ x = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

name: toAdd_one
description: This tool provides a theorem stating that converting the multiplicative identity to the additive form results in the additive identity.
conditions: α must have a multiplicative structure
α must have an additive structure
The type α must have a zero element
function_body:
theorem toAdd_one [Zero α] : toAdd (1 : Multiplicative α) = 0 :=
  rfl

name: ofMul_inv
description: This theorem states that for any element x in an involutive monoid α, the value of ofMul x⁻¹ is equal to the negative of ofMul x.
conditions: x is an element of α
function_body: theorem ofMul_inv [Inv α] (x : α) : ofMul x⁻¹ = -ofMul x := rfl

name: toMul_neg
description: A tool to prove that the additive inverse of any element in an Abelian group with a multiplicative inverse is equal to its multiplicative inverse.
conclusions: The additive inverse of any element x in α is equal to the multiplicative inverse of the additive element x
function_body:
theorem toMul_neg [Inv α] (x : Additive α) : toMul (-x) = (toMul x)⁻¹ :=
  rfl

name: ofAdd_neg
description: A tool that encapsulates the theorem stating that the inverse of the additive inverse of a number is equal to the original number.
conditions: Existence of an additive inverse for the number
Existence of a multiplicative inverse for the number
conclusions: The inverse of the additive inverse of a number is equal to the original number
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_neg [Neg α] (x : α) : ofAdd (-x) = (ofAdd x)⁻¹ :=
  rfl

name: toAdd_inv
description: This tool provides a method to determine the additive inverse of the multiplicative inverse of a number, showing that it is equivalent to the negation of the additive inverse of the number.
conditions: The number must have an additive inverse.
The number must have a multiplicative inverse.
conclusions: The additive inverse of the multiplicative inverse of a number is the negation of the additive inverse of the number.
function_body:
theorem toAdd_inv [Neg α] (x : Multiplicative α) : toAdd x⁻¹ = -(toAdd x) :=
  rfl

name: ofAdd_sub
description: This tool provides a theorem proof stating that for integers x and y, the difference between x and y equals their quotient provided certain conditions are met.
function_body:
theorem ofAdd_sub [Sub α] (x y : α) : ofAdd (x - y) = ofAdd x / ofAdd y :=
  rfl

name: toAdd_div
description: A tool to find the additive inverse of a quotient in multiplicative notation.
conditions: x and y are elements of a type with a subtstraction operation defined after converting from multiplicative to additive notation using toAdd.
conclusions: The additive inverse of the quotient x / y is equal to toAdd x - toAdd y.
function_body:
theorem toAdd_div [Sub α] (x y : Multiplicative α) : toAdd (x / y) = toAdd x - toAdd y :=
  rfl

name: ofMul_div
description: This theorem states that for any two rational numbers x and y, the ofMul of x divided by y is equal to the ofMul of x minus the ofMul of y.
conditions: x and y are rational numbers
conclusions: ofMul (x / y) = ofMul x - ofMul y
function_body:
theorem ofMul_div [Div α] (x y : α) : ofMul (x / y) = ofMul x - ofMul y :=
rfl

name: toMul_sub
description: Encapsulates the relationship between the subtraction in the additive group and division in the multiplicative group within a division ring.
conditions: x and y are elements of the additive group of α
conclusions: toMul (x - y) is equal to toMul x / toMul y

theorem toMul_sub [Div α] (x y : Additive α) : toMul (x - y) = toMul x / toMul y :=

name: ULift.one_down
description: This tool verifies that for any type α with an instance of One, the down function when applied to the value 1 of the ULift α type returns 1.
conditions: There is an instance of One for the type α
function_body: theorem one_down [One α] : (1 : ULift α).down = 1 := rfl

name: ULift.mul_down
description: This tool provides a theorem that shows the down operator distributes over multiplication in a monoid.
conditions: α is a monoid under multiplication

theorem mul_down [Mul α] : (x * y).down = x.down * y.down :=
  rfl

name: ULift.div_down
description: The ULift.div_down tool verifies that the floor of the quotient of two numbers is equal to the quotient of the floors of those numbers under integer division.
function_body: theorem div_down [Div α] : (x / y).down = x.down / y.down := rfl

name: ULift.inv_down
description: This tool states and proves that the inverse of a down function is the down function of the inverse.
conditions: The function must be a down function.
conclusions: The inverse of the down function is equal to the down function of the inverse.
function_body: theorem inv_down [Inv α] : x⁻¹.down = x.down⁻¹ := rfl

name: ULift.smul_down
description: This tool relates the scalar multiplication of a lifted instance to the scalar multiplication of its base instance in the context of algebraic structures.
conditions: α and β are SMul instances
b is of type ULift β
conclusions: The down function of a • b equals a • b.down
function_body:
theorem smul_down [SMul α β] (a : α) (b : ULift.{v} β) : (a • b).down = a • b.down :=
  rfl

name: ULift.pow_down
description: A tool that demonstrates how the lift and down operations interact with exponentiation in type theory.
conditions: $a$ is an element of the lift of a type $\alpha$ to a type $\beta$

theorem pow_down [Pow α β] (a : ULift.{v} α) (b : β) : (a ^ b).down = a.down ^ b :=
  rfl

name: ULift.up_natCast
description: A theorem that states casting a natural number (n) into a type α using the function 'up' results in the original natural number n.
conditions: There is a type α that supports natural number casting (NatCast α).
n is a natural number (n : ℕ).
function_body:
theorem up_natCast [NatCast α] (n : ℕ) : up (n : α) = n :=
  rfl

description: This tool proves that the function 'up' which lifts an integer 'n' to a type 'α' returns the same integer 'n' when 'α' is an integer type.
conditions: α is an integer type (IntCast α)
function_body:
theorem up_intCast [IntCast α] (n : ℤ) : up (n : α) = n :=
  rfl

name: ULift.down_natCast
description: This theorem states that for any natural number \( n \) lifted to a type \( \alpha \) using ULift, the down function will return \( n \).
function_body: theorem down_natCast [NatCast α] (n : ℕ) : down (n : ULift α) = n := rfl

name: ULift.down_intCast
description: A theorem that states that applying the `down` function to a value of type `ULift α` when α is ℤ results in the value itself.
function_body:
theorem down_intCast [IntCast α] (n : ℤ) : down (n : ULift α) = n :=
  rfl

name: pow_le_pow_of_le_left'
description: This tool proves that for any positive real numbers a and b, if a ≤ b, then a^i ≤ b^i for any natural number i.
conditions: a and b are positive real numbers
conclusions: a^i ≤ b^i for any natural number i
function_body:
theorem pow_le_pow_of_le_left' [CovariantClass M M (swap (· * ·)) (· ≤ ·)] {a b : M} (hab : a ≤ b) : ∀ i : ℕ, a ^ i ≤ b ^ i
  | 0 => by simp
  | k + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ, pow_succ]
    exact mul_le_mul' hab (pow_le_pow_of_le_left' hab k)

name: one_le_pow_of_one_le
description: This tool verifies that for any real number `a` at least 1 and any natural number `n`, the power `a^n` is also at least 1.
function_body:
theorem one_le_pow_of_one_le {a : ℝ} (H : 1 ≤ a) : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ a ^ n 
  | 0 => by simp 
  | k + 1 => by 
    rw [pow_succ] 
    exact mul_le_mul H (one_le_pow_of_one_le H k)

name: pow_le_one'
description: A theorem that states if a number 'a' is less than or equal to 1, then raises 'a' to a positive integer power 'n' will also be less than or equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem pow_le_one' {a : M} (H : a ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) : a ^ n ≤ 1 :=
  @one_le_pow_of_one_le' Mᵒᵈ _ _ _ _ H n

name: pow_le_pow'
description: A tool that states if 'a' is a positive real number and 'n' and 'm' are natural numbers such that 'n' is less than or equal to 'm', then 'a' raised to the power of 'n' is less than or equal to 'a' raised to the power of 'm'.
conditions: a is a positive real number
n and m are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem pow_le_pow' {a : M} {n m : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (h : n ≤ m) : a ^ n ≤ a ^ m :=
  let ⟨k, hk⟩ := Nat.le.dest h
  calc
    a ^ n ≤ a ^ n * a ^ k := le_mul_of_one_le_right' (one_le_pow_of_one_le' ha _)
    _ = a ^ m := by rw [← hk, pow_add]

name: pow_le_pow_of_le_one'
description: A tool that proves if a is less than or equal to 1, and n and m are natural numbers with n <= m, then a^m <= a^n
conditions: n and m are natural numbers
function_body:
theorem pow_le_pow_of_le_one' {a : M} {n m : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ 1) (h : n ≤ m) : a ^ m ≤ a ^ n :=
  @pow_le_pow' Mᵒᵈ _ _ _ _ _ _ ha h

name: one_lt_pow'
description: This tool proves that for any number a greater than 1 and any positive natural number k, a raised to the power of k is greater than 1.
function_body:
theorem one_lt_pow' {a : M} (ha : 1 < a) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) : 1 < a ^ k := by
  rcases Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero hk with ⟨l, rfl⟩
  clear hk
  induction' l with l IH
  · rw [pow_succ]; simpa using ha
  · rw [pow_succ]
    exact one_lt_mul'' ha IH

name: pow_lt_one
description: This tool validates that for a positive real number 'a' less than 1, and any positive integer 'k', the power 'a^k' is less than 1.
conditions: a is a positive real number less than 1
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_one {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (ha' : a < 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) : a ^ k < 1 :=
  by { have h : 1 - a ≠ 0, linarith, rw [sub_lt_self_iff (pow_pos ha k)], exact ha' }

name: pow_lt_pow'
description: A tool to prove that for any numbers a > 1 and integers n < m, the inequality a^n < a^m holds by leveraging the growth property of exponential functions.
function_body: theorem pow_lt_pow' [CovariantClass M M (· * ·) (· < ·)] {a : M} {n m : ℕ} (ha : 1 < a) (h : n < m) : a ^ n < a ^ m := by rcases Nat.le.dest h with ⟨k, rfl⟩; clear h rw [pow_add, pow_succ', mul_assoc, ← pow_succ] exact lt_mul_of_one_lt_right' _ (one_lt_pow' ha k.succ_ne_zero)

name: pow_strictMono_left
description: This tool provides a proof for the strict monotonicity of the power function when raising numbers to the power of a number greater than one.
function_body: theorem pow_strictMono_left [CovariantClass M M (· * ·) (· < ·)] {a : M} (ha : 1 < a) : StrictMono ((· ^ ·) a : ℕ → M) := fun _ _ => pow_lt_pow' ha

name: Left.one_le_pow_of_le
description: This tool proves that for any real number x greater than or equal to 1, all natural number powers of x are also greater than or equal to 1, using strong induction.
conclusions: x^n >= 1 for all natural numbers n
function_body:
theorem Left.one_le_pow_of_le (hx : 1 ≤ x) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 1 ≤ x ^ n
  | 0 => (pow_zero x).ge
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact Left.one_le_mul hx <| Left.one_le_pow_of_le hx

name: Left.pow_le_one_of_le
description: This tool uses the principle of mathematical induction to prove that for any x ≤ 1, x raised to any natural number power n is also less than or equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem Left.pow_le_one_of_le (hx : x ≤ 1) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, x ^ n ≤ 1
  | 0 => (pow_zero _).le
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact Left.mul_le_one hx <| Left.pow_le_one_of_le hx

name: Right.one_le_pow_of_le
description: This tool proves that for any real number x where x >= 1, x raised to the power of any natural number n is also greater than or equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem Right.one_le_pow_of_le (hx : 1 ≤ x) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 1 ≤ x ^ n
  | 0 => (pow_zero _).ge
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact Right.one_le_mul hx <| Right.one_le_pow_of_le hx

name: Right.pow_le_one_of_le
description: This tool verifies that if a number x is less than or equal to 1, then x raised to any natural number n is still less than or equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem Right.pow_le_one_of_le (hx : x ≤ 1) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, x ^ n ≤ 1
  | 0 => (pow_zero _).le
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact Right.mul_le_one hx <| Right.pow_le_one_of_le hx

name: StrictMono.pow_right'
description: A tool to prove that the n-th power of a strictly monotone function is also strictly monotone.
conditions: f is a strictly monotone function
function_body:
theorem StrictMono.pow_right' (hf : StrictMono f) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → StrictMono fun a => f a ^ n
  | 0, hn => (hn rfl).elim
  | 1, _ => by simpa
  | Nat.succ <| Nat.succ n, _ => by
    simp_rw [pow_succ _ (n + 1)]
    exact hf.mul' (StrictMono.pow_right' hf n.succ_ne_zero)

name: pow_strictMono_right'
description: This theorem states that for any non-zero natural number n, the function mapping a to a^n is strictly increasing.
conditions: n is a non-zero natural number
a and b are elements of M with a < b
conclusions: a^n < b^n, making f(a) = a^n strictly increasing
function_body: theorem pow_strictMono_right' {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : StrictMono fun a : M => a ^ n := strictMono_id.pow_right' hn

name: Monotone.pow_right
description: This tool proves that if a function f is monotone, then raising f to any natural number power also results in a monotone function.
conclusions: f^n is monotone for all n ∈ ℕ
function_body:
theorem Monotone.pow_right {f : β → M} (hf : Monotone f) : ∀ n : ℕ, Monotone fun a => f a ^ n
  | 0 => by simpa using monotone_const
  | n + 1 => by
    simp_rw [pow_succ]
    exact hf.mul' (Monotone.pow_right hf _)

name: pow_mono_right
description: Proves that for any natural number n, the function f(x) = x^n is monotonically increasing.
conclusions: The function f(x) = x^n is increasing for all x in the given set
function_body:
theorem pow_mono_right (n : ℕ) : Monotone fun a : M => a ^ n :=
  monotone_id.pow_right _

name: Left.pow_lt_one_of_lt
description: This theorem establishes that for any positive integer n and any real number x less than 1, x raised to the power of n is still less than 1. The proof is carried out using mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem Left.pow_lt_one_of_lt [CovariantClass M M (· * ·) (· < ·)] {n : ℕ} {x : M} (hn : 0 < n)
    (h : x < 1) : x ^ n < 1 :=
  Nat.le_induction ((pow_one _).trans_lt h)
    (fun n _ ih => by
      rw [pow_succ]
      exact mul_lt_one h ih)
    _ (Nat.succ_le_iff.2 hn)

name: Right.pow_lt_one_of_lt
description: This tool proves that if a real number x is less than 1, then x raised to the power of any positive integer n is also less than 1.
function_body: theorem Right.pow_lt_one_of_lt [CovariantClass M M (swap (· * ·)) (· < ·)] {n : ℕ} {x : M} (hn : 0 < n) (h : x < 1) : x ^ n < 1 := Nat.le_induction ((pow_one _).trans_lt h) (fun n _ ih => by rw [pow_succ] exact Right.mul_lt_one h ih) _ (Nat.succ_le_iff.2 hn)

name: one_le_pow_iff
description: This tool verifies that for a positive integer \(n\) and a real number \(x\), \(1 \le x^n\) if and only if \(1 \le x\).
conclusions: 1 ≤ x^n if and only if 1 ≤ x
function_body:
theorem one_le_pow_iff {x : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 1 ≤ x ^ n ↔ 1 ≤ x :=
  ⟨le_imp_le_of_lt_imp_lt fun h => pow_lt_one' h hn, fun h => one_le_pow_of_one_le' h n⟩

name: pow_le_one_iff
description: Encapsulates the theorem which states for an element x in a monoid M and a positive natural number n, x^n ≤ 1 if and only if x ≤ 1.
conditions: x is an element of a monoid M
n is a positive natural number
conclusions: x^n ≤ 1 if and only if x ≤ 1
function_body:
theorem pow_le_one_iff {x : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : x ^ n ≤ 1 ↔ x ≤ 1 :=
  @one_le_pow_iff Mᵒᵈ _ _ _ _ _ hn

name: one_lt_pow_iff
description: This tool proves that for a non-zero integer exponent, a base x raised to the power n is greater than 1 if and only if the base x itself is greater than 1.
function_body: theorem one_lt_pow_iff {x : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 1 < x ^ n ↔ 1 < x := lt_iff_lt_of_le_iff_le (pow_le_one_iff hn)

name: pow_lt_one_iff
description: Determines if x is less than 1 based on the condition that x raised to a positive power n is less than 1.
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_one_iff {x : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : x ^ n < 1 ↔ x < 1 :=
  lt_iff_lt_of_le_iff_le (one_le_pow_iff hn)

name: pow_eq_one_iff
description: This tool proves that for an element x of a monoid M and a nonzero natural number n, x raised to the power of n equals 1 if and only if x equals 1.
function_body:
theorem pow_eq_one_iff {x : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : x ^ n = 1 ↔ x = 1 := by
  simp only [le_antisymm_iff]
  rw [pow_le_one_iff hn, one_le_pow_iff hn]

name: pow_le_pow_iff'
description: This tool compares two exponential expressions with the same base and determines the relationship between their exponents.
function_body: theorem pow_le_pow_iff' (ha : 1 < a) : a ^ m ≤ a ^ n ↔ m ≤ n := (pow_strictMono_left ha).le_iff_le

name: pow_lt_pow_iff'
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that for any real number a greater than 1, a raised to the power m is less than a raised to the power n if and only if m is less than n.
conclusions: a^m < a^n if and only if m < n
function_body: theorem pow_lt_pow_iff' (ha : 1 < a) : a ^ m < a ^ n ↔ m < n := (pow_strictMono_left ha).lt_iff_lt

name: lt_of_pow_lt_pow'
description: This tool proves that if the n-th power of a number a is less than the n-th power of a number b for some positive integer n, then the number a is less than the number b.
conditions: a and b are elements of a set with an ordering (typically the real numbers or any ordered set)
function_body:
theorem lt_of_pow_lt_pow' {a b : M} (n : ℕ) : a ^ n < b ^ n → a < b :=
  (pow_mono_right _).reflect_lt

name: min_lt_of_mul_lt_sq
description: Determines that if the product of two values is less than the square of a third value, then the minimum of the two values is less than the third value.
function_body:
theorem min_lt_of_mul_lt_sq {a b c : M} (h : a * b < c ^ 2) : min a b < c := by
  simpa using min_lt_max_of_mul_lt_mul (h.trans_eq <| pow_two _)

name: lt_max_of_sq_lt_mul
description: This tool leverages a theorem that states if the square of 'a' is less than the product of 'b' and 'c', then 'a' must be less than the maximum of 'b' and 'c'. It employs a proof by contradiction.
function_body:
theorem lt_max_of_sq_lt_mul {a b c : M} (h : a ^ 2 < b * c) : a < max b c := by
  simpa using min_lt_max_of_mul_lt_mul ((pow_two _).symm.trans_lt h)

name: le_of_pow_le_pow'
description: Determines that if a positive integer raised to a power is less than or equal to another positive integer raised to the same power, then the original integer is less than or equal to the other integer.
function_body:
theorem le_of_pow_le_pow' {a b : M} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ^ n ≤ b ^ n → a ≤ b :=
  (pow_strictMono_right' hn).le_iff_le.1

name: min_le_of_mul_le_sq
description: This tool establishes that if the product of two numbers is less than or equal to the square of another number, then the minimum of those two numbers is less than or equal to the square root of that number.
function_body:
theorem min_le_of_mul_le_sq {a b c : M} (h : a * b ≤ c ^ 2) : min a b ≤ c := by
  simpa using min_le_max_of_mul_le_mul (h.trans_eq <| pow_two _)

name: le_max_of_sq_le_mul
description: This tool proves that if the square of a number is less than or equal to the product of two other numbers, then the first number is less than or equal to the maximum of the latter two numbers.
function_body:
theorem le_max_of_sq_le_mul {a b c : M} (h : a ^ 2 ≤ b * c) : a ≤ max b c := by
  simpa using min_le_max_of_mul_le_mul ((pow_two _).symm.trans_le h)

name: Left.pow_lt_one_iff'
description: This theorem states that for any positive integer n and real number x such that x < 1, it follows that x^n < 1.
conditions: x is a real number such that x < 1
function_body:
theorem Left.pow_lt_one_iff' [CovariantClass M M (· * ·) (· < ·)] {n : ℕ} {x : M} (hn : 0 < n) :
    x ^ n < 1 ↔ x < 1 :=
  haveI := covariantClass_le_of_lt M M (· * ·)
  pow_lt_one_iff hn.ne'

name: Left.pow_lt_one_iff
description: This tool proves that for a type M with a left action of a monoid and a linear order, x^n < 1 if and only if x < 1 for all positive integers n.
conditions: M is a type equipped with a left action of a monoid
x is an element of M
conclusions: x^n < 1 if and only if x < 1
function_body: theorem Left.pow_lt_one_iff [CovariantClass M M (· * ·) (· < ·)] {n : ℕ} {x : M} (hn : 0 < n) : x ^ n < 1 ↔ x < 1 := Left.pow_lt_one_iff' hn

name: Right.pow_lt_one_iff
description: Determines that for any number x and a positive integer n, x^n < 1 if and only if x < 1.
conclusions: x < 1 if and only if x^n < 1
function_body: theorem Right.pow_lt_one_iff [CovariantClass M M (swap (· * ·)) (· < ·)] {n : ℕ} {x : M} (hn : 0 < n) : x ^ n < 1 ↔ x < 1 := ⟨fun H => not_le.mp fun k => haveI := covariantClass_le_of_lt M M (swap (· * ·)) H.not_le <| Right.one_le_pow_of_le k, Right.pow_lt_one_of_lt hn⟩

name: one_le_zpow
description: A theorem that proves if 1 ≤ x and 0 ≤ n, then 1 ≤ x^n for any element x in a group G.
function_body:
theorem one_le_zpow {x : G} (H : 1 ≤ x) {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) : 1 ≤ x ^ n := by
  lift n to ℕ using hn
  rw [zpow_ofNat]
  apply one_le_pow_of_one_le' H

name: CanonicallyOrderedCommSemiring.pow_pos
description: This theorem states that if a is a positive real number, then its power a^n is also positive for any natural number n.
conditions: a is a positive real number
function_body:
theorem pow_pos {a : R} (H : 0 < a) (n : ℕ) : 0 < a ^ n :=
  pos_iff_ne_zero.2 <| pow_ne_zero _ H.ne'

name: zero_pow_le_one
description: This tool proves that for any natural number n, 0^n is less than or equal to 1 using mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem zero_pow_le_one : ∀ n : ℕ, (0 : R) ^ n ≤ 1
  | 0 => (pow_zero _).le
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [zero_pow n.succ_pos]
    exact zero_le_one

name: pow_add_pow_le
description: This tool proves that for non-negative real numbers x and y, and a positive integer n, the sum of their nth powers is less than or equal to the nth power of their sum.
function_body:
theorem pow_add_pow_le (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) (hn : n ≠ 0) : x ^ n + y ^ n ≤ (x + y) ^ n := by
  rcases Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero hn with ⟨k, rfl⟩
  induction' k with k ih;
  · have eqn : Nat.succ Nat.zero = 1 := rfl
    rw [eqn]
    simp only [pow_one, le_refl]
  · let n := k.succ
    have h1 := add_nonneg (mul_nonneg hx (pow_nonneg hy n)) (mul_nonneg hy (pow_nonneg hx n))
    have h2 := add_nonneg hx hy
    calc
      x ^ n.succ + y ^ n.succ ≤ x * x ^ n + y * y ^ n + (x * y ^ n + y * x ^ n) := by
        rw [pow_succ _ n, pow_succ _ n]
        exact le_add_of_nonneg_right h1
      _ = (x + y) * (x ^ n + y ^ n) := by
        rw [add_mul, mul_add, mul_add, add_comm (y * x ^ n), ← add_assoc, ← add_assoc,
          add_assoc (x * x ^ n) (x * y ^ n), add_comm (x * y ^ n) (y * y ^ n), ← add_assoc]
      _ ≤ (x + y) ^ n.succ := by
        rw [pow_succ _ n]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (ih (Nat.succ_ne_zero k)) h2

name: pow_le_one
description: This tool proves that if a number 'a' is between 0 and 1, then raising 'a' to any natural number power results in a value that is also less than or equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem pow_le_one : ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 ≤ a) (_ : a ≤ 1), a ^ n ≤ 1
  | 0, _, _ => (pow_zero a).le
  | n + 1, h₀, h₁ => (pow_succ' a n).le.trans (mul_le_one (pow_le_one n h₀ h₁) h₀ h₁)

name: pow_lt_one
description: This tool proves that for a real number 0 ≤ a < 1, \( a^n < 1 \) holds for all natural numbers \( n ≠ 0 \).
conclusions: a^n < 1 for all natural numbers n ≠ 0
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_one (h₀ : 0 ≤ a) (h₁ : a < 1) : ∀ {n : ℕ} (_ : n ≠ 0), a ^ n < 1
  | 0, h => (h rfl).elim
  | n + 1, _ => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact mul_lt_one_of_nonneg_of_lt_one_left h₀ h₁ (pow_le_one _ h₀ h₁.le)

name: one_le_pow_of_one_le
description: This tool proves that for any number a greater than or equal to 1, the power of a to any natural number is also greater than or equal to 1.
conclusions: a^n ≥ 1 for all natural numbers n
function_body:
theorem one_le_pow_of_one_le (H : 1 ≤ a) : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ a ^ n
  | 0 => by rw [pow_zero]
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    simpa only [mul_one] using
      mul_le_mul H (one_le_pow_of_one_le H n) zero_le_one (le_trans zero_le_one H)

name: pow_mono
description: This tool proves the monotonicity (monotone increasing) of the function a^n with respect to n, given that a is greater than or equal to 1.
conclusions: a^n is monotone increasing with respect to n
function_body:
theorem pow_mono (h : 1 ≤ a) : Monotone fun n : ℕ => a ^ n :=
  monotone_nat_of_le_succ fun n => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact le_mul_of_one_le_left (pow_nonneg (zero_le_one.trans h) _) h

name: le_self_pow
description: This tool verifies that for any real number a greater than or equal to 1 and a non-zero integer m, the value of a is less than or equal to a raised to the power m.
function_body:
theorem le_self_pow (ha : 1 ≤ a) (h : m ≠ 0) : a ≤ a ^ m :=
  (pow_one a).symm.trans_le (pow_le_pow ha <| pos_iff_ne_zero.mpr h)

name: pow_le_pow_of_le_left
description: This theorem states that if 0 ≤ a ≤ b, then raising a to any natural number power results in a value less than or equal to raising b to the same power.
conclusions: a^i ≤ b^i for all i ∈ ℕ
function_body:
theorem pow_le_pow_of_le_left {a b : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∀ i : ℕ, a ^ i ≤ b ^ i := by
  intro i
  induction i with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [pow_succ, pow_succ]
    apply mul_le_mul hab
    apply ih
    apply pow_nonneg ha
    apply le_trans ha hab

name: one_lt_pow
description: Proves that if \(a > 1\), then \(a^n > 1\) for all natural numbers \(n\) except 0, using mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem one_lt_pow (ha : 1 < a) : ∀ {n : ℕ} (_ : n ≠ 0), 1 < a ^ n
  | 0, h => (h rfl).elim
  | n + 1, _ => by
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact one_lt_mul_of_lt_of_le ha (one_le_pow_of_one_le ha.le _)

name: pow_lt_pow_of_lt_left
description: This tool verifies that if two real numbers x and y satisfy x < y and x is non-negative, then for any natural number n, x raised to the power n is less than y raised to the power n.
function_body: theorem pow_lt_pow_of_lt_left (h : x < y) (hx : 0 ≤ x) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → x ^ n < y ^ n | 0, hn => by contradiction | n + 1, _ => by simpa only [pow_succ'] using mul_lt_mul_of_le_of_le' (pow_le_pow_of_le_left hx h.le _) h (pow_pos (hx.trans_lt h) _) hx

name: strictMonoOn_pow
description: This tool proves that the function f(x) = x^n is strictly monotone on the set [0, ∞) given that the exponent n is positive.
conclusions: f(x) = x^n is strictly increasing on [0, ∞)
function_body: theorem strictMonoOn_pow (hn : 0 < n) : StrictMonoOn (fun x : R => x ^ n) (Set.Ici 0) := fun _ hx _ _ h => pow_lt_pow_of_lt_left h hx hn

name: pow_strictMono_right
description: This tool proves that the function f(n) = a^n is strictly increasing for any real number a > 1.
conclusions: f(n) = a^n is strictly increasing for n ∈ ℕ
function_body:
theorem pow_strictMono_right (h : 1 < a) : StrictMono fun n : ℕ => a ^ n :=
  have : 0 < a := zero_le_one.trans_lt h
  strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ fun n => by
    simpa only [one_mul, pow_succ] using mul_lt_mul h (le_refl (a ^ n)) (pow_pos this _) this.le

name: pow_lt_pow
description: This tool proves that for a base greater than 1, raising it to a smaller exponent results in a smaller value compared to raising it to a larger exponent.
function_body: theorem pow_lt_pow (h : 1 < a) (h2 : n < m) : a ^ n < a ^ m := pow_strictMono_right h h2

name: pow_lt_pow_iff
description: This tool determines the relationship between exponents and the order of powers for a real number greater than 1.
conditions: a is a real number greater than 1
conclusions: a^n < a^m if and only if n < m
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_pow_iff (h : 1 < a) : a ^ n < a ^ m ↔ n < m :=
  (pow_strictMono_right h).lt_iff_lt

name: pow_le_pow_iff
description: This tool determines the condition under which the inequality a^n ≤ a^m holds, given a > 1, encapsulating the relationship between the exponents and the base.
conclusions: a^n ≤ a^m if and only if n ≤ m
function_body:
theorem pow_le_pow_iff (h : 1 < a) : a ^ n ≤ a ^ m ↔ n ≤ m :=
  (pow_strictMono_right h).le_iff_le

name: self_lt_pow
description: A theorem that shows for any a > 1 and m > 1, a is less than a raised to the power of m.
function_body:
theorem self_lt_pow (h : 1 < a) (h2 : 1 < m) : a < a ^ m := by
  calc
    a = a ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
    _ < a ^ m := pow_lt_pow h h2

name: self_le_pow
description: This theorem states that for any real number a greater than or equal to 1, and any positive integer m, the value a is less than or equal to a raised to the power of m.
function_body:
theorem self_le_pow (h : 1 ≤ a) (h2 : 1 ≤ m) : a ≤ a ^ m :=
  le_self_pow h <| Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mp h2

name: strictAnti_pow
description: This tool proves that for any real number 'a' such that 0 < a < 1, the sequence 'a^n' is strictly decreasing.
function_body:
theorem strictAnti_pow (h₀ : 0 < a) (h₁ : a < 1) : StrictAnti fun n : ℕ => a ^ n :=
  strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => by
    simpa only [pow_succ, one_mul] using mul_lt_mul h₁ le_rfl (pow_pos h₀ n) zero_le_one

name: pow_lt_pow_iff_of_lt_one
description: This tool demonstrates the relationship between powers of a real number in the interval (0, 1). Specifically, it shows that for 0 < a < 1, a^m < a^n if and only if n < m.
conditions: m and n are real numbers
conclusions: a^m < a^n if and only if n < m
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_pow_iff_of_lt_one (h₀ : 0 < a) (h₁ : a < 1) : a ^ m < a ^ n ↔ n < m :=
  (strictAnti_pow h₀ h₁).lt_iff_lt

name: pow_lt_pow_of_lt_one
description: A theorem that states if 0 < a < 1, then for any natural numbers i and j where i < j, a^j < a^i.
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_pow_of_lt_one (h : 0 < a) (ha : a < 1) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i < j) : a ^ j < a ^ i :=
  (pow_lt_pow_iff_of_lt_one h ha).2 hij

name: pow_lt_self_of_lt_one
description: This tool verifies that if a real number is between 0 and 1, then raising it to any power greater than 1 will yield a value less than the original number.
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_self_of_lt_one (h₀ : 0 < a) (h₁ : a < 1) (hn : 1 < n) : a ^ n < a :=
  calc
    a ^ n < a ^ 1 := pow_lt_pow_of_lt_one h₀ h₁ hn
    _ = a := pow_one _

name: sq_pos_of_pos
description: This tool provides a mathematical theorem stating that the square of a positive real number is also positive.
conditions: a is a positive real number
conclusions: a^2 is a positive real number
function_body:
theorem sq_pos_of_pos (ha : 0 < a) : 0 < a ^ 2 := by
  rw [sq]
  exact mul_pos ha ha

name: pow_bit0_pos_of_neg
description: This tool proves that raising a negative number to a power that is a power of 2 results in a positive number.
function_body:
theorem pow_bit0_pos_of_neg (ha : a < 0) (n : ℕ) : 0 < a ^ bit0 n := by
  rw [pow_bit0']
  exact pow_pos (mul_pos_of_neg_of_neg ha ha) _

name: pow_bit1_neg
description: This theorem demonstrates that if a number 'a' is less than zero, then raising 'a' to the power of 2^n yields a positive value, refuting the claim that such a number could be negative.
function_body:
theorem pow_bit1_neg (ha : a < 0) (n : ℕ) : a ^ bit1 n < 0 := by
  rw [bit1, pow_succ]
  exact mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos ha (pow_bit0_pos_of_neg ha n)

name: sq_pos_of_neg
description: This tool proves that the square of a negative number is positive.
function_body:
theorem sq_pos_of_neg (ha : a < 0) : 0 < a ^ 2 :=
  pow_bit0_pos_of_neg ha 1

name: pow_le_one_iff_of_nonneg
description: This tool verifies that for a nonnegative real number a and a nonzero natural number n, the inequality a^n ≤ 1 holds if and only if a ≤ 1.
conditions: a is a nonnegative real number
n is a nonzero natural number
conclusions: a^n ≤ 1 if and only if a ≤ 1
function_body:
theorem pow_le_one_iff_of_nonneg {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ^ n ≤ 1 ↔ a ≤ 1 := by
  refine' ⟨_, pow_le_one n ha⟩
  rw [← not_lt, ← not_lt]
  exact mt fun h => one_lt_pow h hn

name: one_le_pow_iff_of_nonneg
description: Determines if the nonnegative base raised to a positive natural number is at least one if and only if the base itself is at least one.
conditions: a is a nonnegative real number
n is a nonzero natural number
function_body:
theorem one_le_pow_iff_of_nonneg {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 1 ≤ a ^ n ↔ 1 ≤ a := by 
  refine' ⟨_, fun h => one_le_pow_of_one_le h n⟩ 
  rw [← not_lt, ← not_lt] 
  exact mt fun h => pow_lt_one ha h hn

name: one_lt_pow_iff_of_nonneg
description: This tool provides a theorem that shows the equivalence between 1 being less than a^n and 1 being less than a for any nonnegative real number a other than 1.
conditions: a is a nonnegative real number (0 ≤ a)
conclusions: 1 < a^n if and only if 1 < a
function_body:
theorem one_lt_pow_iff_of_nonneg {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 1 < a ^ n ↔ 1 < a :=
  lt_iff_lt_of_le_iff_le (pow_le_one_iff_of_nonneg ha hn)

name: pow_lt_one_iff_of_nonneg
description: This tool states that for a non-negative real number and a non-zero natural number, the number raised to the power of the natural number is less than 1 if and only if the number itself is less than 1.
conditions: a is a non-negative real number
n is a non-zero natural number
conclusions: a^n < 1 if and only if a < 1
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_one_iff_of_nonneg {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ^ n < 1 ↔ a < 1 :=
  lt_iff_lt_of_le_iff_le (one_le_pow_iff_of_nonneg ha hn)

name: sq_le_one_iff
description: A theorem establishing the equivalence between a^2 ≤ 1 and a ≤ 1 for non-negative real numbers.
function_body:
theorem sq_le_one_iff {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : a ^ 2 ≤ 1 ↔ a ≤ 1 :=
  pow_le_one_iff_of_nonneg ha (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)

name: sq_lt_one_iff
description: A theorem stating that if a is non-negative, then a^2 < 1 if and only if a < 1.
conclusions: a^2 < 1 if and only if a < 1
function_body:
theorem sq_lt_one_iff {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : a ^ 2 < 1 ↔ a < 1 :=
  pow_lt_one_iff_of_nonneg ha (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)

name: one_le_sq_iff
description: This tool verifies if a real number a, given that it is non-negative, satisfies the condition that 1 is less than or equal to the square of a if and only if 1 is less than or equal to a.
function_body:
theorem one_le_sq_iff {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : 1 ≤ a ^ 2 ↔ 1 ≤ a :=
  one_le_pow_iff_of_nonneg ha (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)

name: one_lt_sq_iff
description: This theorem establishes the equivalence of 1 < a^2 and 1 < a for a non-negative real number.
conditions: a is a non-negative real number (0 ≤ a)
conclusions: 1 < a^2 if and only if 1 < a
function_body:
theorem one_lt_sq_iff {a : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : 1 < a ^ 2 ↔ 1 < a :=
  one_lt_pow_iff_of_nonneg ha (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)

name: pow_left_inj
description: A tool that verifies if two non-negative real numbers raised to the power of a positive integer are equal, then the numbers themselves are equal.
conditions: x and y are non-negative real numbers
conclusions: x^n = y^n if and only if x = y
function_body:
theorem pow_left_inj {x y : R} {n : ℕ} (Hxpos : 0 ≤ x) (Hypos : 0 ≤ y) (Hnpos : 0 < n) :
  x ^ n = y ^ n ↔ x = y :=
  (@strictMonoOn_pow R _ _ Hnpos).eq_iff_eq Hxpos Hypos

name: lt_of_pow_lt_pow
description: This tool demonstrates that if the nth power of a is less than the nth power of b, and b is non-negative, then a must be less than b.
function_body:
theorem lt_of_pow_lt_pow {a b : R} (n : ℕ) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (h : a ^ n < b ^ n) : a < b :=
  lt_of_not_ge (fun hn => not_lt_of_ge (pow_le_pow_of_le_left hb hn _) h)

name: le_of_pow_le_pow
description: This tool verifies that if a raised to the power of n is less than or equal to b raised to the power of n, for natural number n, non-negative b, and positive n, then a is less than or equal to b.
conditions: a^n ≤ b^n for some natural number n
function_body:
theorem le_of_pow_le_pow {a b : ℝ} (n : ℕ) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hn : 0 < n) (h : a ^ n ≤ b ^ n) : a ≤ b :=
  le_of_not_lt (fun h1 => not_le_of_lt (pow_lt_pow_of_lt_left h1 hb hn) h)

name: sq_eq_sq
description: A tool that shows the equivalence between \(a^2 = b^2\) and \(a = b\) for nonnegative real numbers.
conditions: a and b are nonnegative real numbers
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_sq {a b : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : a ^ 2 = b ^ 2 ↔ a = b :=
  pow_left_inj ha hb (by decide)

name: lt_of_mul_self_lt_mul_self
description: Determines that if the square of one non-negative real number is less than the square of another, then the first number is less than the second.
conditions: a and b are non-negative real numbers
function_body:
theorem lt_of_mul_self_lt_mul_self (hb : 0 ≤ b) : a * a < b * b → a < b := by
  simp_rw [← sq]
  exact lt_of_pow_lt_pow _ hb

name: pow_abs
description: Verifies that the absolute value of any real number raised to any natural number power equals the absolute value of the number raised to that power.
function_body:
theorem pow_abs (a : R) (n : ℕ) : |a| ^ n = |a ^ n| :=
  ((absHom.toMonoidHom : R →* R).map_pow a n).symm

name: abs_neg_one_pow
description: A tool to prove that the absolute value of (-1) raised to any integer power is always equal to 1.
function_body: theorem abs_neg_one_pow (n : ℕ) : |(-1 : R) ^ n| = 1 := by rw [← pow_abs, abs_neg, abs_one, one_pow]

name: abs_pow_eq_one
description: This tool provides a theorem that establishes the equivalence between |a^n| = 1 and |a| = 1 for a real number a and a positive integer n.
function_body:
theorem abs_pow_eq_one (a : R) {n : ℕ} (h : 0 < n) : |a ^ n| = 1 ↔ |a| = 1 := by
  convert pow_left_inj (abs_nonneg a) zero_le_one h
  exacts [(pow_abs _ _).symm, (one_pow _).symm]

name: pow_bit0_nonneg
description: This tool proves that for any non-negative real number a and natural number n, the expression a^(2n) is non-negative.
conditions: a is a non-negative real number (a ≥ 0)
n is a natural number (n ∈ ℕ)
function_body:
theorem pow_bit0_nonneg (a : R) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ a ^ bit0 n := by
  rw [pow_bit0]
  exact mul_self_nonneg _

name: sq_nonneg
description: This tool validates that the square of any real number is non-negative.
conclusions: The square of a is non-negative
function_body: theorem sq_nonneg (a : R) : 0 ≤ a ^ 2 := pow_bit0_nonneg a 1

name: pow_bit0_pos
description: This tool determines that raising any nonzero real number to the power of a nonzero even exponent results in a positive number.
function_body:
theorem pow_bit0_pos {a : R} (h : a ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) : 0 < a ^ bit0 n :=
  (pow_bit0_nonneg a n).lt_of_ne (pow_ne_zero _ h).symm

name: sq_pos_of_ne_zero
description: This tool establishes that if a real number, a, is non-zero, then its square, a^2, is positive.
conditions: a is a non-zero real number
function_body:
theorem sq_pos_of_ne_zero (a : R) (h : a ≠ 0) : 0 < a ^ 2 :=
  pow_bit0_pos h 1

name: pow_bit0_pos_iff
description: A theorem that states for a real number a and a positive integer n, a^(2^n) is positive if and only if a is nonzero.
conclusions: a^(2^n) > 0 if and only if a ≠ 0
function_body:
theorem pow_bit0_pos_iff (a : R) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 0 < a ^ bit0 n ↔ a ≠ 0 := by
  refine' ⟨fun h => _, fun h => pow_bit0_pos h n⟩
  rintro rfl
  rw [zero_pow (Nat.zero_lt_bit0 hn)] at h
  exact lt_irrefl _ h

name: sq_pos_iff
description: A tool that verifies the positivity of the square of a real number is equivalent to the number being nonzero.
conclusions: 0 < a^2 if and only if a ≠ 0
function_body: theorem sq_pos_iff (a : R) : 0 < a ^ 2 ↔ a ≠ 0 := pow_bit0_pos_iff a one_ne_zero

name: sq_abs
description: A tool that proves the relationship between the square of the absolute value of a real number and the square of the number itself.
function_body: theorem sq_abs (x : R) : |x| ^ 2 = x ^ 2 := by simpa only [sq] using abs_mul_abs_self x

name: abs_sq
description: This tool proves that the absolute value of the square of any real number is equal to the square of that number.
function_body: theorem abs_sq (x : R) : |x ^ 2| = x ^ 2 := by simpa only [sq] using abs_mul_self x

name: sq_lt_sq
description: This theorem establishes that for any real numbers x and y, x^2 is less than y^2 if and only if the absolute value of x is less than the absolute value of y.
conditions: x and y are real numbers
conclusions: x^2 < y^2 if and only if |x| < |y|
function_body:
theorem sq_lt_sq : x ^ 2 < y ^ 2 ↔ |x| < |y| := by
  simpa only [sq_abs] using
    (@strictMonoOn_pow R _ _ two_pos).lt_iff_lt (abs_nonneg x) (abs_nonneg y)

name: sq_lt_sq'
description: A tool to prove that if -y < x < y, then x^2 < y^2 using a proof by contradiction.
function_body:
theorem sq_lt_sq' (h1 : -y < x) (h2 : x < y) : x ^ 2 < y ^ 2 :=
  sq_lt_sq.2 (lt_of_lt_of_le (abs_lt.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩) (le_abs_self _))

name: sq_le_sq
description: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the squares of two real numbers and their absolute values.
conditions: x and y are real numbers
conclusions: x² ≤ y² if and only if |x| ≤ |y|
function_body:
theorem sq_le_sq : x ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2 ↔ |x| ≤ |y| := by
  simpa only [sq_abs] using
    (@strictMonoOn_pow R _ _ two_pos).le_iff_le (abs_nonneg x) (abs_nonneg y)

name: sq_le_sq'
description: A theorem that states if a value x is between -y and y, then the square of x is less than or equal to the square of y.
function_body:
theorem sq_le_sq' (h1 : -y ≤ x) (h2 : x ≤ y) : x ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2 :=
  sq_le_sq.2 (le_trans (abs_le.mpr ⟨h1, h2⟩) (le_abs_self _))

name: abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq
description: This tool handles proving that the absolute value of x is less than y given that the square of x is less than the square of y and y is non-negative.
function_body:
theorem abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq (h : x ^ 2 < y ^ 2) (hy : 0 ≤ y) : |x| < y := by
  rwa [← abs_of_nonneg hy, ← sq_lt_sq]

name: abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq'
description: A theorem stating that for real numbers x and y, if x^2 < y^2 and y is nonnegative, then -y < x < y.
function_body:
theorem abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq' (h : x ^ 2 < y ^ 2) (hy : 0 ≤ y) : -y < x ∧ x < y :=
  abs_lt.mp <| abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq h hy

name: abs_le_of_sq_le_sq
description: A tool that determines if the absolute value of x is less than or equal to y given that the square of x is less than or equal to the square of y and y is non-negative.
function_body:
theorem abs_le_of_sq_le_sq (h : x ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2) (hy : 0 ≤ y) : |x| ≤ y := by
  rwa [← abs_of_nonneg hy, ← sq_le_sq]

name: abs_le_of_sq_le_sq'
description: A theorem that proves if the square of a real number x is less than or equal to the square of another real number y and y is nonnegative, then x lies within the interval [-y, y].
conditions: x and y are real numbers
function_body:
theorem abs_le_of_sq_le_sq' (h : x ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2) (hy : 0 ≤ y) : -y ≤ x ∧ x ≤ y :=
  abs_le.mp <| abs_le_of_sq_le_sq h hy

name: sq_eq_sq_iff_abs_eq_abs
description: A tool to determine the equivalence between squares of two numbers being equal and their absolute values being equal.
function_body:
theorem sq_eq_sq_iff_abs_eq_abs (x y : R) : x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ↔ |x| = |y| := by
  simp only [le_antisymm_iff, sq_le_sq]

name: sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between the inequality x^2 ≤ 1 and the absolute value inequality |x| ≤ 1.
conditions: x is a real number (x ∈ R)
function_body:
theorem sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one (x : R) : x ^ 2 ≤ 1 ↔ |x| ≤ 1 := by
  simpa only [one_pow, abs_one] using @sq_le_sq _ _ x 1

name: sq_lt_one_iff_abs_lt_one
description: This tool proves the equivalence between the statement that the square of a number is less than one and the absolute value of that number being less than one.
function_body:
theorem sq_lt_one_iff_abs_lt_one (x : R) : x ^ 2 < 1 ↔ |x| < 1 := by
  simpa only [one_pow, abs_one] using @sq_lt_sq _ _ x 1

name: one_le_sq_iff_one_le_abs
description: This tool verifies that the square of a real number is at least one if and only if the absolute value of that number is at least one.
conditions: x is a real number (x ∈ R)
function_body:
theorem one_le_sq_iff_one_le_abs (x : R) : 1 ≤ x ^ 2 ↔ 1 ≤ |x| := by
  simpa only [one_pow, abs_one] using @sq_le_sq _ _ 1 x

name: one_lt_sq_iff_one_lt_abs
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between 1 being less than the square of a real number and 1 being less than the absolute value of that real number.
function_body:
theorem one_lt_sq_iff_one_lt_abs (x : R) : 1 < x ^ 2 ↔ 1 < |x| := by
  simpa only [one_pow, abs_one] using @sq_lt_sq _ _ 1 x

name: pow_four_le_pow_two_of_pow_two_le
description: This tool demonstrates that if the square of a number is less than or equal to another number, then the fourth power of the first number is less than or equal to the square of the second number.
function_body:
theorem pow_four_le_pow_two_of_pow_two_le {x y : R} (h : x ^ 2 ≤ y) : x ^ 4 ≤ y ^ 2 :=
  (pow_mul x 2 2).symm ▸ pow_le_pow_of_le_left (sq_nonneg x) h 2

name: two_mul_le_add_sq
description: Proves that for any real numbers a and b, the product of 2, a, and b is less than or equal to the sum of the squares of a and b.
function_body:
theorem two_mul_le_add_sq (a b : R) : 2 * a * b ≤ a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 :=
  sub_nonneg.mp ((sub_add_eq_add_sub _ _ _).subst ((sub_sq a b).subst (sq_nonneg _)))

name: pow_pos_iff
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that for any positive integer n, a^n > 0 if and only if a > 0.
conclusions: a^n > 0 if and only if a > 0
function_body:
theorem pow_pos_iff (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < a ^ n ↔ 0 < a := by
  simp_rw [zero_lt_iff, pow_ne_zero_iff hn]

name: pow_lt_pow_succ
description: A tool that proves for any number 'a' greater than 1, the number raised to the power 'n' is less than the same number raised to the power 'n+1'.
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_pow_succ (ha : 1 < a) : a ^ n < a ^ n.succ := by
  rw [← one_mul (a ^ n), pow_succ]
  exact mul_lt_right₀ _ ha (pow_ne_zero _ (zero_lt_one.trans ha).ne')

name: pow_lt_pow₀
description: A tool that proves if a > 1 and m < n, then a^m < a^n using mathematical induction.
function_body:
theorem pow_lt_pow₀ (ha : 1 < a) (hmn : m < n) : a ^ m < a ^ n := by
  induction' hmn with n _ ih
  exacts [pow_lt_pow_succ ha, lt_trans ih (pow_lt_pow_succ ha)]

name: MonoidHom.map_neg_one
description: A tool to determine the value of a function at -1 given specific conditions on the function.
function_body:
theorem map_neg_one : f (-1) = 1 :=
  (pow_eq_one_iff (Nat.succ_ne_zero 1)).1 <| by rw [← map_pow, neg_one_sq, map_one]

name: MonoidHom.map_neg
description: This theorem proves that the map_neg function is odd, meaning that for any real number x, applying the function to -x results in the negation of applying the function to x.
conditions: f is a homomorphism from the multiplicative monoid of real numbers to itself
conclusions: f(-x) = -f(x) for any real number x
function_body: theorem map_neg (x : R) : f (-x) = -f (x) := by rw [← neg_one_mul, map_mul, map_neg_one, one_mul]

name: MonoidHom.map_sub_swap
description: A theorem that shows for a function f(x), the identity f(x-y) = f(y-x) holds by utilizing the property of negative arguments.
function_body: theorem map_sub_swap (x y : R) : f (x - y) = f (y - x) := by rw [← map_neg, neg_sub]

name: Commute.inv_inv
description: This tool verifies that if two elements commute, then their inverses also commute.
conditions: Elements a and b commute: ab = ba
function_body:
theorem inv_inv : Commute a b → Commute a⁻¹ b⁻¹ :=
  SemiconjBy.inv_inv_symm

name: Commute.inv_inv_iff
description: This tool provides a theorem that states the inverses of elements a and b in a group commute if and only if the elements a and b themselves commute.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group.
conclusions: a⁻¹ commutes with b⁻¹ if and only if a commutes with b.
function_body:
theorem inv_inv_iff : Commute a⁻¹ b⁻¹ ↔ Commute a b :=
  SemiconjBy.inv_inv_symm_iff

name: Commute.div_mul_div_comm
