There must exist a multiplicative inverse for the element a.
function_body:
theorem mul_inv_cancel_comm : a * b * a⁻¹ = b :=
  (Commute.all a b).mul_inv_cancel

name: mul_inv_cancel_comm_assoc
description: A theorem that shows the cancellation property using the inverse of a number under multiplication, assuming the associativity and commutativity of the multiplication operation.
conditions: a and b are elements of a group
a⁻¹ is the multiplicative inverse of a
function_body:
theorem mul_inv_cancel_comm_assoc : a * (b * a⁻¹) = b :=
  (Commute.all a b).mul_inv_cancel_assoc

name: Set.preimage_one
description: This tool evaluates the preimage of a set under a constant function that maps everything to 1. Depending on whether 1 is in the set, the preimage is either the entire universe or the empty set.
conclusions: If 1 ∈ s, the preimage is the universe; otherwise, it is the empty set
function_body:
theorem Set.preimage_one {α β : Type*} [One β] (s : Set β) [Decidable ((1 : β) ∈ s)] :
    (1 : α → β) ⁻¹' s = if (1 : β) ∈ s then Set.univ else ∅ :=
  Set.preimage_const 1 s

name: MulHom.coe_mul
description: This tool demonstrates that for any two semigroup homomorphisms, their pointwise product is equivalent to the product of their values at each element.
conditions: f and g are semigroup homomorphisms from M to N
conclusions: The pointwise product (f * g) is equivalent to the function that maps each x in M to f(x) * g(x) in N
function_body: theorem coe_mul {M N} {_ : Mul M} {_ : CommSemigroup N} (f g : M →ₙ* N) : (f * g : M → N) = fun x => f x * g x := rfl

name: Pi.mulHom_injective
description: This tool provides a function that ensures the injectivity of a product of monoid homomorphisms if each individual homomorphism is injective.
conditions: f_i is a monoid for all i in I
g_i : γ -> f_i is a monoid homomorphism for all i in I
g_i is injective for all i in I
conclusions: The function g : γ -> Π_{i ∈ I} f_i defined by g(x) = (g_i(x))_{i ∈ I} is injective
function_body: theorem Pi.mulHom_injective {γ : Type w} [Nonempty I] [∀ i, Mul (f i)] [Mul γ] (g : ∀ i, γ →ₙ* f i) (hg : ∀ i, Function.Injective (g i)) : Function.Injective (Pi.mulHom g) := fun x y h => let ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty I› hg i ((Function.funext_iff.mp h : _) i)

name: ProductMonoid
description: A tool that ensures the product of given monoids forms a monoid itself.
conclusions: The product monoid f_1 × f_2 × ... × f_n is a monoid
function_body:
theorem ProductMonoid {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n.succ → Type) [∀ i, Monoid (f i)] : Monoid (Π i, f i) :=
{
  one := fun i => 1,
  mul := fun x y i => x i * y i,
  one_mul := fun x => funext (fun i => one_mul (x i)),
  mul_one := fun x => funext (fun i => mul_one (x i)),
  mul_assoc := fun x y z => funext (fun i => mul_assoc (x i) (y i) (z i))
}

name: OneHom.single_apply
description: This tool demonstrates that the OneHom.single function is equivalent to the mulSingle function for given arguments under specific conditions.
conditions: ∀ i, One <| f i: For all indices i, the value of f i must be an instance of the type class One.
conclusions: OneHom.single f i x = mulSingle i x: The two terms are equal by definition.
function_body: theorem OneHom.single_apply [∀ i, One <| f i] (i : I) (x : f i) : OneHom.single f i x = mulSingle i x := rfl

name: MonoidHom.single_apply
description: This tool ensures that for a given monoid homomorphism, the identity element of the input monoid is mapped to the identity element of the output monoid.
conditions: 1_i is the identity element of monoid i
1_{f(i)} is the identity element of monoid f(i)
conclusions: f(1_i) is the identity element of f(i)
function_body: theorem MonoidHom.single_apply [∀ i, MulOneClass <| f i] (i : I) (x : f i) : MonoidHom.single f i x = mulSingle i x := rfl

name: Pi.mulSingle_sup
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that proves if each f(i) (for i in a set I) is a semilattice with supremum operation and neutral element, then the cartesian product f(i) × f(i) is also a semilattice with a defined supremum operation and neutral element.
conditions: f(i) is a semilattice with a supremum operation ⊔ for every i in set I
f(i) has a neutral element 1 for every i in set I
conclusions: f(i) × f(i) is a semilattice with supremum operation (x, y) ⊔ (y, x) and neutral element (1, 1)
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_sup [∀ i, SemilatticeSup (f i)] [∀ i, One (f i)] (i : I) (x y : f i) :
Pi.mulSingle i (x ⊔ y) = Pi.mulSingle i x ⊔ Pi.mulSingle i y :=
  Function.update_sup _ _ _ _

name: Pi.mulSingle_inf
description: This tool encapsulates the theorem that in a semilattice with infimum, the infimum of the products of an element with two others is equal to the product of that element with the infimum of the two others.
conditions: Existence of an element i and elements x, y in the semilattice
Definition of the product and infimum as in the semilattice
conclusions: The infimum of the product of i with x and the product of i with y is equal to the product of i with the infimum of x and y
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_inf [∀ i, SemilatticeInf (f i)] [∀ i, One (f i)] (i : I) (x y : f i) : 
    Pi.mulSingle i (x ⊓ y) = Pi.mulSingle i x ⊓ Pi.mulSingle i y :=
  Function.update_inf _ _ _ _

name: Pi.mulSingle_mul
description: This tool verifies that for any index `i` from a set `I` and any elements `x` and `y` in the monoid `f i`, the multiplication of these elements respects the `mulSingle` operation.
conditions: `f` is a function from a set `I` to a monoid `M`
conclusions: mulSingle i (x * y) = mulSingle i x * mulSingle i y
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_mul [∀ i, MulOneClass <| f i] (i : I) (x y : f i) :
    mulSingle i (x * y) = mulSingle i x * mulSingle i y :=
  (MonoidHom.single f i).map_mul x y

name: Pi.mulSingle_inv
description: This tool shows that the inverse of the product of a single element in a group is the inverse of the element in the group.
conditions: Existence of a group structure on the elements
conclusions: The inverse of the product of a single element is the inverse of the element
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_inv [∀ i, Group <| f i] (i : I) (x : f i) :
    mulSingle i x⁻¹ = (mulSingle i x)⁻¹ :=
  (MonoidHom.single f i).map_inv x

name: Pi.single_div
description: This theorem shows that for any index i and elements x, y in the group f[i], the mulSingle function applied to the division of x and y is equal to the division of the mulSingle function applied to x and y, leveraging the property that mulSingle is a monoid homomorphism.
conditions: Indices and elements i : I, x, y : f[i]
conclusions: mulSingle i (x / y) = mulSingle i x / mulSingle i y
function_body:
theorem Pi.single_div [∀ i, Group <| f i] (i : I) (x y : f i) : 
  mulSingle i (x / y) = mulSingle i x / mulSingle i y := 
  (MonoidHom.single f i).map_div x y

name: Pi.single_mul
description: A tool to show that for any index in a family of types, the multiplication operator preserves the single element subobject of that type, given that the operator is a monoid homomorphism.
conditions: f is a family of types indexed by a set I
The multiplication operator on each f(i) is a homomorphism of monoids
conclusions: For any i in I, the multiplication operator on f(i) preserves the single element subobject of f(i)
function_body: theorem Pi.single_mul [∀ i, MulZeroClass <| f i] (i : I) (x y : f i) : single i (x * y) = single i x * single i y := (MulHom.single f i).map_mul x y

name: Pi.single_mul_left_apply
description: Given that the function f(i) is zero for all indices i, the result of the product (f(i) * x_i) with any j is zero.
conclusions: (f(i) * x_i) * j = 0 for all i and j
function_body: theorem Pi.single_mul_left_apply [∀ i, MulZeroClass <| f i] (a : f i) : Pi.single i (a * x i) j = Pi.single i a j * x j := (Pi.apply_single (fun i => (· * x i)) (fun _ => zero_mul _) _ _ _).symm

name: Pi.single_mul_right_apply
description: This theorem shows that for a function `f` of type `Pi i, MulZeroClass <| f i`, the equation `Pi.single i (x i * a) j = x j * Pi.single i a j` holds for any `a : f i`.
conditions: f is a function of type `Pi i, MulZeroClass <| f i`
a is an element of `f i`
conclusions: Pi.single i (x i * a) j = x j * Pi.single i a j
function_body: theorem Pi.single_mul_right_apply [∀ i, MulZeroClass <| f i] (a : f i) : Pi.single i (x i * a) j = x j * Pi.single i a j :=  (Pi.apply_single (fun i => (· * ·) (x i)) (fun _ => mul_zero _) _ _ _).symm

name: Pi.single_mul_left
description: This theorem demonstrates that a function f(x) defined as a*x for a given value a and x can be shown to be valid using structural induction.
conditions: The operation * follows the MulZeroClass, which implies multiplication is associative and compatible with zero
function_body: theorem Pi.single_mul_left [∀ i, MulZeroClass <| f i] (a: f i) : Pi.single i (a * x i) = Pi.single i a * x := funext fun _ => Pi.single_mul_left_apply _ _ _ _

name: Pi.single_mul_right
description: This theorem provides the property that multiplying a family of vectors with an indicator function on one index of the product space is commutative.
conditions: f: I -> V is a family of vector spaces
conclusions: x * 1_i = 1_i * x for all i ∈ I
function_body:
theorem Pi.single_mul_right [∀ i, MulZeroClass <| f i] (a : f i) :
  Pi.single i (x i * a) = x * Pi.single i a :=
  funext fun _ => Pi.single_mul_right_apply _ _ _ _

name: Pi.mulSingle_commute
description: A theorem that demonstrates the commutativity of the operations mulSingle for a multiclass function under certain conditions.
conditions: Indices i and j and elements x of f i and y of f j
conclusions: mulSingle i x ∘ mulSingle j y = mulSingle j y ∘ mulSingle i x
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_commute [∀ i, MulOneClass <| f i] :
  Pairwise fun i j => ∀ (x : f i) (y : f j), Commute (mulSingle i x) (mulSingle j y) := by
  intro i j hij x y; ext k
  by_cases h1 : i = k;
  · subst h1
    simp [hij]
  by_cases h2 : j = k;
  · subst h2
    simp [hij]
  simp [h1, h2]

name: Pi.mulSingle_apply_commute
description: This tool ensures that the family of elements x_i multiplied by 1 in a type class C commutes pointwise.
conditions: x_i is a family of elements of a type class C
MulOneClass is implemented for the type class C
Decidable equality is available for the indices i, j
conclusions: The family of elements x_i * 1_C commutes pointwise: (x_i * 1_C) * (x_j * 1_C) = (x_j * 1_C) * (x_i * 1_C) for all i and j
function_body: theorem Pi.mulSingle_apply_commute [∀ i, MulOneClass <| f i] (x : ∀ i, f i) (i j : I) : Commute (mulSingle i (x i)) (mulSingle j (x j)) := by obtain rfl | hij := Decidable.eq_or_ne i j · rfl · exact Pi.mulSingle_commute hij _ _

name: Pi.update_eq_div_mul_mulSingle
description: A tool to establish that updating a function at a certain index with a new value is equivalent to dividing the function by `mulSingle` applied to the original value at that index, and then multiplying by `mulSingle` applied to the new value.
conclusions: Function.update(g, i, x) = (g / mulSingle(i, g(i))) * mulSingle(i, x)
function_body:
theorem Pi.update_eq_div_mul_mulSingle [∀ i, Group <| f i] (g : ∀ i : I, f i) (x : f i) : Function.update g i x = g / mulSingle i (g i) * mulSingle i x := by
  ext j
  rcases eq_or_ne i j with (rfl | h)
  · simp
  · simp [Function.update_noteq h.symm, h]

name: Pi.mulSingle_mul_mulSingle_eq_mulSingle_mul_mulSingle
description: This tool proves that two products of mulSingle elements in a commutative monoid are equal if and only if specific conditions on indices and elements are met.
conditions: u = v and k = n and l = m
u * v = 1 and k = l and m = n
conclusions: (mulSingle_k u : I → M) * mulSingle_l v = mulSingle_m u * mulSingle_n v
function_body:
theorem Pi.mulSingle_mul_mulSingle_eq_mulSingle_mul_mulSingle {M : Type*} [CommMonoid M]
    {k l m n : I} {u v : M} (hu : u ≠ 1) (hv : v ≠ 1) :
    (mulSingle k u : I → M) * mulSingle l v = mulSingle m u * mulSingle n v ↔ 
      k = m ∧ l = n ∨ u = v ∧ k = n ∧ l = m ∨ u * v = 1 ∧ k = l ∧ m = n := by
  refine' ⟨fun h => _, _⟩
  · have hk := congr_fun h k
    have hl := congr_fun h l
    have hm := (congr_fun h m).symm
    have hn := (congr_fun h n).symm
    simp only [mul_apply, mulSingle_apply, if_pos rfl] at hk hl hm hn
    rcases eq_or_ne k m with (rfl | hkm)
    · refine' Or.inl ⟨rfl, not_ne_iff.mp fun hln => (hv _).elim⟩
      rcases eq_or_ne k l with (rfl | hkl)
      · rwa [if_neg hln.symm, if_neg hln.symm, one_mul, one_mul] at hn
      · rwa [if_neg hkl.symm, if_neg hln, one_mul, one_mul] at hl
    · rcases eq_or_ne m n with (rfl | hmn)
      · rcases eq_or_ne k l with (rfl | hkl)
        · rw [if_neg hkm.symm, if_neg hkm.symm, one_mul, if_pos rfl] at hm
          exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hm, rfl, rfl⟩)
        · simp only [if_neg hkm, if_neg hkl, mul_one] at hk
          dsimp at hk
          contradiction
      · rw [if_neg hkm.symm, if_neg hmn, one_mul, mul_one] at hm
        obtain rfl := (ite_ne_right_iff.mp (ne_of_eq_of_ne hm.symm hu)).1
        rw [if_neg hkm, if_neg hkm, one_mul, mul_one] at hk
        obtain rfl := (ite_ne_right_iff.mp (ne_of_eq_of_ne hk.symm hu)).1
        exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hk.trans (if_pos rfl), rfl, rfl⟩)
  · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨h, rfl, rfl⟩)
    · rfl
    · apply mul_comm
    · simp_rw [← Pi.mulSingle_mul, h, mulSingle_one]

name: Function.update_one
description: This tool verifies that updating a constant function that returns 1 at any index to 1 does not change the function's return value.
function_body:
theorem update_one [∀ i, One (f i)] [DecidableEq I] (i : I) : update (1 : ∀ i, f i) i 1 = 1 :=
  update_eq_self i (1 : (a : I) → f a)

name: Function.update_mul
description: This tool proves that updating the pointwise product of two functions at an index with the product of their new values is equivalent to the pointwise product of individually updated functions at that index.
conditions: Both functions f1 and f2 are defined for all i
Updates occur at the same index i
conclusions: update(f1 * f2, i, x1 * x2) = update(f1, i, x1) * update(f2, i, x2)
function_body: theorem update_mul [∀ i, Mul (f i)] [DecidableEq I] (f₁ f₂ : ∀ i, f i) (i : I) (x₁ : f i) (x₂ : f i) : update (f₁ * f₂) i (x₁ * x₂) = update f₁ i x₁ * update f₂ i x₂ := funext fun j => (apply_update₂ (fun _ => (· * ·)) f₁ f₂ i x₁ x₂ j).symm

name: Function.update_inv
description: This tool shows that for an update function of a given function, its inverse is the update of the function's inverse.
conditions: x is an element in the codomain of f
i is in the domain of f
conclusions: The inverse of the update function (f[i <- x]) is equal to the update function of the inverse of f with the same update.
function_body:
theorem update_inv [∀ i, Inv (f i)] [DecidableEq I] (f₁ : ∀ i, f i) (i : I) (x₁ : f i) :
  update f₁⁻¹ i x₁⁻¹ = (update f₁ i x₁)⁻¹ :=
funext fun j => (apply_update (fun _ => Inv.inv) f₁ i x₁ j).symm

name: Function.update_div
description: This tool updates the division of two functions at a given index with the respective elements.
conditions: For each index i, there exists a division operation on f i.
f₁ and f₂ are functions such that for each index i, we have f i.
x₁ and x₂ are elements such that f i x₁ and f i x₂, respectively.
conclusions: update (f₁ / f₂) i (x₁ / x₂) is equal to update f₁ i x₁ / update f₂ i x₂.
function_body:
theorem update_div [∀ i, Div (f i)] [DecidableEq I] (f₁ f₂ : ∀ i, f i) (i : I) (x₁ : f i) (x₂ : f i) : update (f₁ / f₂) i (x₁ / x₂) = update f₁ i x₁ / update f₂ i x₂ :=
  funext fun j => (apply_update₂ (fun _ => (· / ·)) f₁ f₂ i x₁ x₂ j).symm

name: Function.const_eq_one
description: This tool verifies the equivalence between the constant function with value a and the constant function with value 1, under the condition that a equals 1.
conditions: There exists an element a of ι.
The constant function with value a equals the constant function with value 1.
conclusions: Element a must be equal to 1.
function_body:
theorem const_eq_one : const ι a = 1 ↔ a = 1 :=
  @const_inj _ _ _ _ 1

name: Function.const_ne_one
description: A tool that asserts a constant function is not equal to 1 if and only if the value of the function is not equal to 1.
conditions: The function is a constant function
The value of the function is not equal to 1
conclusions: The constant function is not equal to 1
The value of the function is not equal to 1
function_body:
theorem const_ne_one : const ι a ≠ 1 ↔ a ≠ 1 :=
  Iff.not const_eq_one

name: Set.piecewise_mul
description: A tool for proving that the piecewise product of functions is equivalent to the product of piecewise applications of functions over a set.
conditions: Let s be a set with index set I
Let f_1, f_2, g_1, g_2 : I -> ℝ be such that f_1(i), f_2(i), g_1(i), and g_2(i) are all multiplicative
conclusions: The piecewise product of f_1 * f_2 and g_1 * g_2 over set s is equal to the product of the piecewise applications of f_1 and g_1, and f_2 and g_2 over set s
function_body:
theorem Set.piecewise_mul [∀ i, Mul (f i)] (s : Set I) [∀ i, Decidable (i ∈ s)]
    (f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ : ∀ i, f i) :
    s.piecewise (f₁ * f₂) (g₁ * g₂) = s.piecewise f₁ g₁ * s.piecewise f₂ g₂ :=
  s.piecewise_op₂ f₁ _ _ _ fun _ => (· * ·)

name: Set.piecewise_inv
description: This tool provides a theorem for computing the inverse of a piecewise function constructed from invertible functions.
conditions: Functions f and g must be invertible for all x
conclusions: The inverse of s.piecewise(f, g) is s.piecewise(f⁻¹, g⁻¹)
function_body: theorem Set.piecewise_inv [∀ i, Inv (f i)] (s : Set I) [∀ i, Decidable (i ∈ s)] (f₁ g₁ : ∀ i, f i) : s.piecewise f₁⁻¹ g₁⁻¹ = (s.piecewise f₁ g₁)⁻¹ := s.piecewise_op f₁ g₁ fun _ x => x⁻¹

name: divisibility_implies_multiplicative
description: Establishes the divisibility relationships in the context of multiplication, meaning if an integer divides both of two factors, it also divides their product.
conditions: ∀ x, ∀ y, x ∣ y → y ∣ x * z → x ∣ z
function_body: theorem divisibility_implies_multiplicative [∀ i, Div (a * b)] (h₀ : ∀ x, ∀ y, x ∣ y → y ∣ x * z → x ∣ z) : ∀ x, x ∣ a → x ∣ b → x ∣ a * b := by intros x ha hb; exact (h₀ x a ha x b hb)

name: BinaryOperationMonotonicity
description: A tool to verify the monotonicity of the binary operation f∘(x,g) in relation to f, keeping g fixed.
function_body:
theorem BinaryOperationMonotonicity : Monotone (λ x, f∘(x, g)) :=
  assume f1 f2 hf, assume ai bi hle,
  calc
    (f1∘(x,g))(ai) = f1(ai, g(ai)) : rfl
                 ... ≤ f1(bi, g(bi)) : hf
                 ... ≤ f2(bi, g(bi)) : hf
                 ... = (f2∘(x,g))(bi) : rfl

name: Pi.mulSingle_strictMono
description: Proves that a function defined using a strictly monotone function is also strictly monotone.
conditions: f is a strictly monotone function from I to ℝ
i, j ∈ I with i < j
conclusions: The generated function is strictly monotone
function_body:
theorem mulSingle_strictMono : StrictMono (Pi.mulSingle i : f i → ∀ i, f i) :=
  Function.update_strictMono

name: unique_one
description: A tool that proves the default value of a type with a unique element and a one element equals one.
conditions: A type with a unique element
A type with a one element
function_body:
theorem unique_one {α : Type*} [Unique α] [One α] : default = (1 : α) :=
  Unique.default_eq 1

name: Units.val_mk
description: This tool provides the value of Units.mk a b h1 h2, proving that it is equal to a based on the definition of Units.mk.
conditions: a is an element of type α
h1 and h2 are conditions required for Units.mk
conclusions: The value of Units.mk a b h1 h2 is a
function_body:
theorem val_mk (a : α) (b h₁ h₂) : ↑(Units.mk a b h₁ h₂) = a :=
  rfl

name: Units.ext
description: A tool to prove that the value projection function for units is injective, meaning if two units have the same value, they are equal.
function_body:
theorem ext : Function.Injective (val : αˣ → α) 
  | ⟨v, i₁, vi₁, iv₁⟩, ⟨v', i₂, vi₂, iv₂⟩, e => by 
    simp only at e; subst v'; congr; 
    simpa only [iv₂, vi₁, one_mul, mul_one] using mul_assoc i₂ v i₁

name: Units.eq_iff
description: This tool provides an equivalence theorem which states that for members of a type α, a = b if and only if (a : α) = b.
conditions: a and b are members of the type α.
Assume a = b or (a : α) = b.
conclusions: Conclude a = b or (a : α) = b, respectively.
function_body:
theorem eq_iff {a b : αˣ} : (a : α) = b ↔ a = b :=
  ext.eq_iff

name: Units.ext_iff
description: This tool establishes the equivalence between the equality of elements a and b in the universe of types α and their equality within that type.
conditions: a and b are elements in the universe of types α
The type α in which a and b reside is defined
conclusions: a = b if and only if a : α is equal to b
function_body:
theorem ext_iff {a b : αˣ} : a = b ↔ (a : α) = b :=
  eq_iff.symm

name: ShowVariableValue
description: This tool demonstrates that the value of a variable in a valuation function is the variable itself.
conditions: There is a valuation function which is a mapping from variables to values.
The variable is part of the domain of the valuation function.
conclusions: The value of the variable in the valuation function is the variable itself.
function_body:
theorem show_variable_value (valuation: Variable -> Value) (v: Variable) : valuation(v) = v :=
  by definition of valuation

name: Units.copy_eq
description: This tool verifies that copying a unit with specific values, invertibility, and inverse properties results in the original unit.
conclusions: u.copy val hv inv hi = u
function_body: theorem copy_eq (u : αˣ) (val hv inv hi) : u.copy val hv inv hi = u := ext hv
